abstract: This paper introduces a Multi-Agency DisAster Management (MADAM) framework for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-assisted public safety systems, based on the principles of game theory and reinforcement learning. Initially, the information quality and criticality (IQC) provided by each agency to an UAV-assisted public safety network is introduced and quantified, and the concept of Value of Information (VoI) that measures each agency's positive contribution to the overall disaster management process is defined. Based on these, a holistic cost function is adopted by each agency, reflecting its relative abstention from the information provisioning process. Each agency aims at minimizing its personal cost function in order to better contribute to the disaster management. This optimization problem is formulated as a non- cooperative game among the agencies and it is proven to be an exact potential game, thus guaranteeing the existence of at least one Pure Nash Equilibrium (PNE). We propose a binary log- linear reinforcement learning algorithm that converges to the optimal PNE. The performance of the proposed approach is evaluated through modeling and simulation under several scenarios, and its superiority compared to other approaches is demonstrated.

title: Collaborative Opportunistic Maintenance Scheduling for Offshore Wind Farms Considering Cognitive Correction
authors: C. Rong; Z. Xiao; L. Xue; Z. Wu
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: High operation and maintenance (O&M) costs and harsh marine environments pose significant challenges to offshore wind farms (OWFs). Existing maintenance strategies often rely on imperfect state information, leading to sub-optimal scheduling. To address these issues, this paper proposes a dynamic collaborative O&M scheduling framework utilizing a heterogeneous fleet of Crew Transfer Vessels (CTVs) and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). First, a reliability model based on the Weibull distribution is utilized to characterize the degradation process of wind turbines. Second, a cognitive correction mechanism is introduced, where UAV inspections dynamically update belief states and trigger event-driven re-planning when cognitive bias exceeds a safety threshold. Finally, a rolling horizon optimization model based on Deferral Opportunity Cost is established to balance deterministic dispatching costs against probabilistic future risks. Simulation results on a 40-turbine OWF demonstrate that the proposed method reduces total O&M costs significantly compared to blind scheduling and reactive strategies, effectively minimizing downtime while ensuring high reliability.

title: Cognitive-State-Driven LLM Decision Agent for Fault Diagnosis of Rotating Machinery Under Incomplete Evidence
authors: H. Zhou; Z. Zhang; T. Wang; Q. Ni; X. Wang; B. Yang; Y. Lei; K. Feng; Y. -a. Hu
venue: 2026 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety Engineering (SRSE)
abstract: Reliable fault diagnosis of rotating machinery under incomplete evidence involves identifying the fault and determining whether the available evidence is sufficient for a decision. However, existing methods mainly map fixed inputs to fault labels and do not systematically evaluate evidence sufficiency. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a cognitive-state-driven large language model (LLM) decision agent for fault diagnosis under incomplete evidence. First, an evidence-state space and a masked representation organize the available evidence, while a unified diagnostic judge provides calibrated class probabilities and a candidate label. Second, uncertainty, stability, out-of-distribution (OOD), and case-memory signals form an augmented cognitive state that describes the current diagnostic belief and its reliability. Finally, a rule-based expert policy provides reference decisions for supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) adjusts the LLM policy to balance submission, further evidence acquisition, abstention, and expert review. Experiments on 4,018 decisionstate records from the Paderborn University (PU) bearing dataset show that the 14B GRPO policy reduces potentially premature automatic submissions. These cases occur when the model submits a diagnosis even though the reference policy recommends acquiring more evidence, and their number decreases from 181 to 119, corresponding to a relative reduction of 34.3%. The wrong automatic diagnosis rate decreases from 4.16% to 3.56%. These results suggest that the proposed agent achieves a more favorable balance between automatic submission and further evidence acquisition at the decision-state level, thereby supporting more reliable diagnostic decisions.

title: Balancing the Scales: Uncertainty-Aware Two-Stage RL for Multiview Child Malnutrition Screening
authors: M. Khan; M. Vatsa; K. Singh; R. Singh
venue: 2026 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision Workshops (WACVW)
abstract: Childhood malnutrition affects over 150 million children (under 5) globally, yet automated screening systems suffer from overconfident predictions, inability to defer ambiguous cases, and misalignment with clinical workflows. We present a two-stage reinforcement learning framework formulating malnutrition screening as a contextual bandit with explicit deferral. Stage 1 classifies children as healthy, malnourished, or deferred; Stage 2 assigns subtypes when needed. The agent observes fused normalized anthropometric measurements and mean-pooled multi-view CLIP embeddings, with Monte Carlo dropout providing uncertainty estimates guiding deferral decisions. The reward function encodes clinical priorities through false-negative penalties and severity-weighted subtype scoring. Evaluated on 2,389 children with eight pose views, our method achieves 94.3% accuracy and 97.2% specificity, reducing false positive rate by 53.5% versus the best baseline while lowering expert deferral by a relative change of 25.4%. Precision on autonomously resolved cases improves by 5.8%, indicating reduced deferral reflects improved decision quality rather than overconfidence. Robustness analysis confirms stable performance under missing modalities and anthropometric noise, while fairness evaluation shows consistent behavior across gender and age groups. These results demonstrate that reinforcement learning with uncertainty-aware deferral substantially improves deployment efficiency for pediatric malnutrition screening in resource-constrained settings.

title: When Not to Edit: Reliability Diagnostics for Activation-Space Interventions in Language Models
authors: N. Y. A. Osafo; R. Doku; D. B. Rawat
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Information Reuse and Integration for Data Science (IRI)
abstract: Activation-space interventions steer language model behavior by editing hidden states along a concept direction. Existing methods usually ask how strongly to edit, but not whether the direction is reliable enough to edit at all. This is an information-reliability problem: an inferred internal signal is being used to modify generated information, and a mistaken edit can silently reduce utility, invert the target behavior, or introduce cross-concept side effects. We present a preflight diagnostic fingerprint for activation editing, $\left(\kappa^{*}, d_{c}, A\right)$, measuring task-subspace coherence, direction quality, and projection asymmetry. The fingerprint produces a calibrated intervention scale that can be zero, making abstention a firstclass output rather than a failed edit. On GPT-2, the gated projection achieves +53.6% toxicity reduction using five-seed generation means $(p<0.001)$ while incurring $3.3 \times$ less perplexity cost than ungated projection. On gender, the same framework refuses to edit because the direction is one-sided; removing the asymmetry factor over-corrects pronoun skew from 0.704 to 0.017. On Mistral-7B, the framework abstains from projection at all 32 layers $(\kappa^{*} \geq 40$), while an ActAdd sweep can still reduce toxicity, showing that the diagnosis is operator-specific rather than a claim that the concept is uneditable. The contribution is not a stronger universal edit, but a reliability layer that explains when projection is safe, when it should be weakened, and when it should not be used.

title: Techno-Economic Analysis of Smart EV Charging for Expansion Planning Under Uncertainty
authors: S. Giannelos; S. Borozan; A. Moreira; G. Strbac
abstract: The ongoing electrification of transport is expected to lead to a significant load growth, thereby creating the need for network reinforcements, which may be ameliorated by new smart technologies such as the Smart Charging of Electric Vehicles. This paper presents the relation between key techno-economics of this technology such as flexibility, Option Value and investment cost, with the level of network reinforcement necessary to accommodate the uncertain future load growth. Furthermore, the concept of deferral and displacement of conventional network investment in the context of multi-stage expansion planning is formulated and analyzed. The conclusions underline the inverse relationship between Option Value and network reinforcement, and the importance of flexibility in deferring conventional reinforcement. Overall, in-depth sensitivity analyses recognize the impact that Smart Charging can have on generating economic savings in power systems.

title: Calibrated and Selective Visual State Diagnosis for Fused Magnesium Furnaces Based on Deep Convolutional Stochastic Configuration Networks
authors: X. Zhang; J. Yang; H. Lei; W. Li; C. Yu
venue: 2026 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety Engineering (SRSE)
abstract: Reliable visual diagnosis of fused magnesium furnace (FMF) states requires accurate classification and confidence estimates that support safe decisions under visually coupled operating conditions and field disturbances. To address this requirement, this paper develops a calibrated and selective diagnosis framework based on a deep convolutional stochastic configuration network (DCSCN). The DCSCN incrementally constructs a compact convolutional representation through a stochastic configuration mechanism, avoiding backpropagation-based optimization of convolutional kernel parameters. Temperature scaling is incorporated as a post-hoc calibration strategy to adjust the sharpness of Softmax probabilities without changing class predictions. A rejection-enabled selective diagnosis mechanism separates state prediction from decision acceptance, and risk-coverage analysis quantifies the trade-off between automatic diagnosis and manual review. Finally, an exploratory mechanism-aware response module groups accepted convolutional kernels according to FMF-related visual patterns and evaluates their contribution to confidence-based rejection. Experiments on 6,661 FMF images with four operating states show that DCSCN achieves 94.89% accuracy and 94.63% macro-F1, while five-fold out-of-fold temperature scaling reduces clean-image ECE from 51.20% to 1.03%. Calibrated maximum softmax probability (MSP) obtains an AURC of 0.004664 and 99.62% accepted-sample accuracy at 80% coverage. Under seven synthetic corruption families and five severity levels, the added task-level audit reports at severity level 5 a macro-averaged corrupted-image accuracy of 71.28%, calibrated ECE of 21.08%, AURC of 0.2127, and 76.93% accepted-sample accuracy at 80% coverage. These results characterize how prediction, confidence, and rejection behavior change as visual disturbances intensify.

title: Reducing Hallucinations in Oncology Question Answering Using Confidence-Gated Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: J. T J; N. Rajagopalan; S. Gopal
venue: 2026 International Conference on Smart Communication and Sustainable Technologies (ICSCST)
abstract: Hallucinations in LLMs are a major issue in developing medical question-answering systems, as the creation of false information can lead to serious safety risks. The Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) model reduces this issue by relying on external knowledge sources. However, in traditional RAG, it is still possible to generate responses even when there is weak or irrelevant evidence.This paper aims to present a novel RAG model that uses cross-encoder re-ranking in conjunction with confidence-gated abstention to ensure that responses are only generated when there is enough evidence. The model was tested using 62 oncology-related questions obtained from a dataset of cancer information in Japanese. The experiment was conducted using closed-domain retrieval of Cancer Information Service (CIS) database information and open-domain retrieval of Google search results. The generative model used in this experiment was GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.The experiment was conducted, and the results show that the proposed model significantly reduces hallucinations compared to traditional RAG. The experiment using open-domain retrieval showed a reduction in conditional hallucinations from 28.0% to 8.82% for GPT-3.5 and from 26.7% to 2.17% for GPT-4. The experiment conducted in this paper proved that combining semantic re-ranking with confidence-gated abstention improves the reliability of AI-based medical information systems.

title: Cognition-Aware LLM Assistance for Light and Full Post-Editing: Cognitive Load Profiling and Adaptive Intervention From Keystroke Dynamics
authors: R. Du; R. Lu
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can improve machine-translation post-editing, but always-on assistance ignores whether support is needed at a given moment and can introduce unnecessary interruption or over-reliance. This problem is amplified by light post-editing (LPE) and full post-editing (FPE), which impose different quality targets and revision demands. We propose a cognition-aware LLM assistance framework that uses non-intrusive keystroke dynamics to connect trial-level workload grounding with selective adaptive intervention. The framework learns task-conditioned hierarchical representations that separate translator-level behavioral profiles from a latent within-trial workload-evidence trajectory, using post-task NASA-TLX only as training-time weak supervision. It then performs profile-calibrated online estimation with explicit uncertainty and abstention and applies a cognition-gated policy that selects the minimum useful assistance level. Evaluation combines a controlled English–Chinese LPE/FPE study with 64 translators and 1,536 sessions (CALPE-64) with three public translation-process resources. On CALPE-64, the proposed estimator achieves a session-level Macro-F1 of 0.781 and an ECE of 0.041. In the held-out human–LLM comparison, aggregate COMET reaches 0.837/0.872 for LPE/FPE while observed editing time and post-task NASA-TLX are lower than in the principal static and always-on conditions. Participant-level mixed-effects models, using translator and source as repeated-observation structure, confirm the primary time and workload contrasts after multiplicity correction. A separate temporally aligned validation check shows moderate within-participant convergence between the latent evidence trajectory and sparse short-horizon mental-effort probes, while matched-budget random-timing and text/QE timing controls are evaluated as offline mechanism diagnostics rather than counterfactual human outcomes. The local trajectory, behavioral recovery time, and unnecessary-intervention rate are therefore interpreted as model-derived operational evidence, not independent moment-to-moment cognitive ground truth. These results support conservative, minimum-necessary assistance while bounding stronger claims about the unique causal role of cognition-aware timing.

title: Fingerprint-Based Selective Rejection for Improving Reliability Under Adversarial Attacks
authors: D. -C. Asimopoulos; V. Vitsas; P. Radoglou-Grammatikis; D. Pliatsios; G. T. Papadopoulos; S. Goudos; T. Lagkas; E. K. Markakis; P. Sarigiannidis
venue: 2026 15th International Conference on Modern Circuits and Systems Technologies (MOCAST)
abstract: Adversarial examples can severely degrade the reliability of deep neural networks, often driving accuracy close to random guessing under strong attacks. In this work, we propose a lightweight, training-free defense based on input fingerprinting and selective rejection. Instead of attempting to robustly classify every input, the method estimates a compact set of fingerprint features capturing prediction confidence, stability under test-time augmentation, and simple signal statistics, and rejects samples deemed unreliable. Experiments on GTSRB with a ResNet-18 classifier under multiple white-box and black-box attacks show that the proposed policy substantially improves accuracy on accepted samples, preserves high reliability on clean data, and almost completely filters out strong optimization-based attacks, at the cost of reduced coverage. The results highlight the practicality of fingerprint-based selective defenses as a complementary reliability layer for safety-critical vision systems.

title: CLARITY: An End-to-End Retrieval-Augmented Generation Pipeline for Ontology-Aligned Industrial Device Auto-Configuration
authors: A. G. Ganie; S. Ezzini; M. Nouioua
abstract: Commissioning an industrial field device still requires an automation engineer to locate the correct manual, extract dozens of protocol-specific parameters (register maps, node identifiers, station addresses, baud rates), and transcribe them into a supervisory system, a workflow that is slow, expensive, and vulnerable to transcription errors whose consequences range from silent data loss to unsafe actuator behavior. This paper presents CLARITY (Context-aware LLM-Assisted Retrieval and Intelligent Auto-configuraTion sYstem), a fully on-premises pipeline that automates this workflow for Modbus, OPC UA, Profibus DP, and CANopen devices. CLARITY chunks device manuals into a hybrid knowledge base combining 1024-dimensional BGE-M3 dense embeddings, BM25 sparse retrieval, and an ontology-graph term boost fused by Reciprocal Rank Fusion; reranks candidates with a sigmoid-normalized cross-encoder; guards a local llama3.1:8b generator with a two-stage abstention gate (rerank-score threshold and IRI resolution ratio); validates generated JSON-LD configurations against protocol-specific SHACL shapes; and deploys through protocol adapters with post-deployment read-back verification. We contribute a component-wise evaluation methodology with evidence-grounded relevance labels and release the full harness. On a 71-chunk corpus with 28 field-level queries, hybrid retrieval with reranking reaches HitRate@10 of 0.964 and MRR@10 of 0.625; rerank scores of documented and undocumented queries separate by a factor of 8.6 with no overlap, so a wide threshold band yields perfect abstention decisions. The generator attains micro field-level F1 = 0.867 with a systematic failure isolated to the OPC UA schema, a defect that component-wise evaluation localizes to the generator and its validation shape rather than retrieval, and that read-back verification catches in every run. Across 15 end-to-end runs on an H100 GPU (a deliberately small benchmark, whose success rates we therefore report with 95% Wilson confidence intervals), documented devices are commissioned in 2.6 to 6.6 seconds with no unsafe writes (0/15; upper 95% bound 0.20) and every failing run terminating in an explicit, machine-readable failure signal (7/7 detected). Modbus and OPC UA are exercised over live network I/O with read-back, whereas Profibus DP and CANopen are validated structurally without bus I/O; all generation uses a single local open-weights model (llama3.1:8b); holding retrieval and validation fixed and swapping only the generator, four open on-premises models all attain field-level F1 between 0.83 and 0.97, indicating the accuracy is a property of the pipeline rather than of one model. A case study then applies the pipeline to a Universal Robots UR5e collaborative robot, with the vendor’s published manuals as the only corpus and a physics-simulated UR5e behind the vendor’s documented Modbus register map as a live deployment target: all three commissioning runs deploy the correct four-register configuration with field-level F1 = 1.0 and pass sentinel, read-back, physical-consistency, and liveness checks, while retrieval quality drops sharply on the vendor’s table-heavy documents and the benchmark-calibrated abstention threshold does not transfer, requiring recalibration from the measured score separation of the new corpus. We argue that this defense-in-depth safety profile, correct behavior of the whole despite an imperfect generator, is the property industrial adoption actually requires, and we characterize its cost, latency, and limits.

title: Drone Assisted Remote Wellness Monitoring Using RGB Camera
authors: E. B. Tuncarslan; I. Yilmaz
venue: 2026 14th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abstract: In remote rural regions and severe weather conditions (e.g., snowstorms and floods), emergency response teams may be delayed or unable to reach patients in time. This motivates drone-assisted remote triage workflows where a firstresponse UAV provides early situational and physiological telemetry to a command center. We present a practical RGB camerabased wellness monitoring pipeline that estimates physiological indicators from video via remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) and motion-derived signals. Unlike accuracy-only approaches, the proposed system targets safety-critical operation by integrating explicit quality gating and a refusal policy to avoid wrong-but-confident outputs under adverse capture conditions (motion, unstable sampling, intermittent face loss, or illumination drift). The pipeline consists of face ROI extraction, POS-inspired signal projection, temporal stabilization, and an interpretable Signal Quality Score (SQS) used for selective publishing. In a pilot real-time capture $\log (\mathrm{N}=3448 \text{JSONL}$ rows; effective median capture rate $\approx 3.72 \text{FPS}$), the system achieves high heartrate telemetry availability (97.71 % coverage) while transparently abstaining on insufficient-evidence segments with explicit reason codes. Since the pilot operates at substantially lower frame rates than typical rPPG settings, we emphasize safety-first availability under strict gating rather than clinical-grade accuracy, and conservatively disable HRV reporting under low-FPS conditions. Failure-mode analysis indicates that dominant rejections are driven by sampling instability and missing respiration evidence. The proposed design supports drone-enabled telehealth triage, where reliability, interpretability, and honest abstention are critical for operational decision-making.

title: Post-Earthquake Building Damage Assessment Using Ordinal Risk and Uncertainty-Aware Classification on Edge Devices
authors: Z. Elmi; S. Elmi; S. Elmi
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Rapid post-earthquake screening of damaged buildings is critical for search-and-rescue prioritization, safety zoning, and early reconstruction planning, yet expert visual inspection remains slow and difficult to scale. We present a deploymentoriented multimodal framework that combines ground-level RGB imagery with vibration and acoustic measurements to estimate ordinal building risk on edge devices. The model integrates lightweight modality-specific encoders, compact late fusion, an all-threshold ordinal prediction head, and uncertainty-aware selective prediction via Monte Carlo dropout and temperature scaling. Because paired field recordings are unavailable, the sensor channels are generated through physics-based simulations conditioned on damage severity; the study should therefore be interpreted as a controlled proof of concept rather than a fully field-validated multimodal benchmark. On the hybrid evaluation set, the proposed model achieves 87.3% accuracy with a mean ordinal error of 0.18, while uncertainty-based abstention improves selective accuracy to 91.4% at 90% coverage. Edge profiling shows real-time single-pass inference with latencies of 50 ms on Jetson Xavier AGX and 120 ms on Jetson Nano. These results support the feasibility of uncertainty-aware multimodal ordinal screening under embedded deployment constraints.

title: Cache-Aware Transformer-Based Scheduling for LLM-Driven IoT Workflows in Multi-Clouds
authors: J. Zhang; L. Mashayekhy
abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into Internet-of-Things (IoT) ecosystems has enabled users to issue high-level natural-language intents that are automatically translated into fine-grained, serverless workflows using protocols such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP). These workflows span heterogeneous multi-cloud platforms, where effective scheduling must account for latency, cost, platform failures, and opportunities for cache reuse. Traditional scheduling heuristics and existing reinforcement learning methods fall short in these highly dynamic environments, especially when decisions must be made online. We propose CATS, a Cache-Aware Transformer Scheduler, trained using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) for adaptive placement and deferral of serverless function executions. CATS models dynamic system conditions, including per-platform failure probabilities, critical-path dependencies, and cache-hit likelihoods, within a Transformer-based policy architecture that learns when to defer execution to exploit cache reuse without incurring excessive delay. We evaluate CATS using a custom event-driven simulator under realistic workload traces. Compared to benchmarks, CATS reduces makespan by up to 30 %, computational cost by 40 %, and retries by over 50 %, while maintaining low scheduling latency suitable for real-time deployment. This work establishes a new direction for reinforcement learning-based orchestration of LLM-driven IoT workflows across dynamic, failure-prone multi-cloud environments.

title: Reliability Aware Fake News Detection: A Survey of Temporal Modeling, Multimodal Fusion, and Uncertainty Estimation
authors: C. Hari Nainyar Pillai; S. Padmavathi
venue: 2026 International Conference on Next Generation Electronics (NELEX)
abstract: The rapid dissemination of misinformation on social media has spurred extensive research on automated fake news detection. Despite recent advancements in deep learning that have enhanced benchmark accuracy, a substantial gap persists between laboratory performance and real-world applicability. This survey offers a taxonomy-driven review of fake news detection methodologies and categorizes existing approaches into content-centric, context-centric, and reliabilitycentric paradigms. Content-based models utilize textual semantics through machine learning and transformer architectures but often depend on static representation. Context-centric approaches incorporate propagation dynamics using graph neural networks and temporal modeling but frequently rely on discrete time snapshots that hinder early detection under irregular diffusion patterns. Multimodal fusion methods integrate semantic and contextual signals; however, naive and confidence-unaware fusion strategies introduce additional vulnerabilities into the model. The survey further explores uncertainty quantification frameworks, including Bayesian methods and evidential deep learning, underscoring the importance of selective abstention and human-in-the-loop moderation for a trustworthy deployment. Two systemic limitations are identified: the discrete-time bottleneck in propagation modeling and the reliability deficit caused by overconfident inference. This study concludes by outlining the open challenges in early detection, cross-platform generalization, adversarial robustness, and uncertainty-aware decision support, emphasizing the need to transition from accuracy-driven classification to reliability-aware misinformation detection systems.

title: Navigating the Certainty Gap: The Hydraulic Effect of Evidence-Constrained LLMs in Professional Decision-Making
authors: F. Gundidza; M. Kikuchi; T. Ozono
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in high-stakes environments, including infrastructure auditing, medical assessment, legal analysis, and peer review. However, these failures arise less from knowledge limitations than from systematic misinterpretation of modality (fact vs. possibility) and unstable decision commitment, leading to two opposing failure modes: false confirmations (over-commitment) and over-abstention (excessive conservatism). To address this, we propose the Evidence–Constrained (EC) Framework, a structured paradigm for regulating LLM decision boundaries through two complementary mechanisms: a Modality Filter (“the Brake”), which enforces strict separation between factual and conditional evidence, and a Normalcy Rule (“the Accelerator”), which enables inference of non-events from routine reporting structures. These terms are used as analytical metaphors describing opposing influences on commitment behavior rather than literal computational operators. We evaluate the framework through a cross-domain experimental study spanning construction, medical, legal, and peer-review tasks, compared against domain-informed human evaluation. Results reveal a systematic trade-off phenomenon, termed “Hydraulic Effect”, where reducing false confirmations increases abstention, reaching up to 35%. We further identify recurring cross-domain failure patterns, including temporal-modality confusion, lexical overheating, and the Condition Precedent Gap. Rather than yielding a single configuration that is uniformly optimal across the evaluated benchmark, the EC framework exposes a persistent trade-off between decision safety and coverage, suggesting that reliable LLM deployment may require explicit calibration of commitment thresholds under uncertainty. These findings provide exploratory guidance for the design of uncertainty-aware LLM workflows. The reported results should be interpreted as evidence from controlled behavioral experiments on carefully selected ambiguity-sensitive benchmark cases rather than as estimates of real-world deployment performance.

title: Harnessing Explainable AI and Biomarker Insights for Robust Breast Cancer Detection
authors: T. Mahbub; R. Parvin; T. Ahmed; R. R. Ridoy
venue: 2025 IEEE International Women in Engineering (WIE) Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (WIECON-ECE)
abstract: Breast cancer remains one of the most common causes of cancer death worldwide, emphasizing the need to spot it early and accurately. The paper aims to detect early of breast cancer by the predictive performance of 11 models including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest(RF), AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, K-Nearest Neighbor and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) on Coimbra breast cancer dataset ($\mathbf{n} \bold{=} \mathbf{1 1 6}$). Data preprocessing dealt with outliers by cross-module treatment and feature scaling. We next performed Boruta-based feature selection, finding that what was most relevant biomarkers but likely just under threshold levels included age, BMI, HOMA, Resistin and glucose. Model evaluation was completed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1score, ROC-AUC, calibration curves and Brier scores. GBM achieved the highest accuracy (96%) with well calibrated probability estimates, while KNN and other boosting methods also performed well. A selective prediction framework with confidence threshold ($\tau$) was implemented to improve clinical practicality, allowing for 10% automation of case classification and expert review for the remaining 90% with uncertain forecasts. Explainability was dealt with using SHAP, PDP, and ICE analysis, with glucose and Resistin emerging as the major influencing biomarkers all along, consistent with established medical knowledge. The results indicate that the combination of ensemble learning, selective prediction, and interpretability techniques offers a robust method for biomarker-based breast cancer detection which is readily applicable in clinical practice.

title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Label Chest X-ray Screening: Temperature Scaling and Risk–Coverage Analysis on NIH14
authors: F. Yasmin; M. S. U. M. Antor; S. Khan; N. K. Podder; M. S. Biswas; S. M. A. Uddin
venue: 2026 International Conference on Power, Electronics, Communications, Computing, and Intelligent Infrastructure (PECCII)
abstract: Multi-label chest X-ray screening systems are important in the clinical workflow, and confidence is a necessity when deploying this technology. A model that is highly discriminating may still be miscalibrated to produce overconfident errors which decrease safety and trust. We learn about confidence-sensitive multi-label screening on the NIH ChestX-ray14 data set through the combination of post-hoc calibration and selective prediction analysis. On an initially reproducible ConvNeXt multi-label baseline, we initially report good discrimination performance, with best validation macro AUC of 0.835 and micro AUC of 0.883, and test micro of 0.848 and test macro of 0.796. We also present bootstrap uncertainty of the summary measures, where AUC means equal 0.796 (95 percent interval: 0.7890.803). Thereafter we perform temperature scaling to calibrate logits on a held-out validation set, and evaluate reliability with metrics of calibration and reliability diagrams. We use safe usage under uncertainty by analyzing selective prediction in risk– coverage curves to understand how not using in situations of uncertainty can limit expected risk at the cost of controlling the proportion of predictions retained. Generally, the paper presents a fully operationalized confidence assessment protocol of multi-label screening of chest X-rays with insights on both practical calibration and selective deployment.

title: Distribution network capacity support from flexible smart multi-energy districts
authors: E. A. Martínez Ceseña; P. Mancarella
venue: 2016 IEEE PES Transmission & Distribution Conference and Exposition-Latin America (PES T&D-LA)
abstract: This paper explores from a techno-economic perspective the value of increasing distribution network capacity via Demand Side Response (DSR) services provided by smart multi-energy systems enabled by an intelligent information platform (i.e., the District Information Modelling and Management for Energy Reduction (DIMMER) platform under development in the homonymous European project). More specifically, the potential of smart multi-energy systems comprising gas boilers, Electric Heat Pumps (EHP) Combined Heat and Power (CHP) and a smart information platform to provide distribution network capacity is explored. For this purpose, a multi-energy district operation optimization approach coupled with a distribution network planning framework is proposed. The district operation model identifies the behavior of end-users who may aim at minimizing their energy costs and/or trade capacity with DNOs. The network planning framework calculates the value for DNOs from additional network capacity provided by customers. The methodology is illustrated via a real UK multi-energy district at the University of Manchester and the relevant electricity, heat and gas networks. The results highlight that the flexibility inherent in multi-energy systems can provide significant economic benefits for both end-users and DNOs.

title: Distribution network support from multi-energy demand side response in smart districts
authors: E. A. Martínez Ceseña; P. Mancarella
venue: 2016 IEEE Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT-Asia)
abstract: This work investigates from a techno-economic perspective the potential for groups of smart buildings distributed throughout an area to provide Demand Side Response (DSR) as a means to increase electricity distribution network capacity. More specifically, intelligent multi-energy flows between buildings within a smart district are optimized with the aim of reducing energy costs for end-users and network costs for Distribution Network Operators (DNOs). For this purpose, an optimization methodology that captures the impacts of DSR by explicitly modelling (ii) interactions between different energy vectors through an integrated electricity-heat-gas model, (ii) security limits and (iii) DNO investment decisions and preferred deployment of DSR, is proposed. The methodology is illustrated with a real UK multi-energy district where an intelligent information platform (i.e., the District Information Modelling and Management for Energy Reduction (DIMMER) platform under development in the homonymous European project) is being tested. The significant flexibility of the smart district to provide DSR services without compromising end-user comfort levels (i.e., avoiding load curtailment) by intelligently exchanging different energy vectors is demonstrated. The results highlight a strong business case for DSR, as the associated deployment costs are minimal thanks to the flexibility of the smart district, while network savings are significant.

title: Raceline-Informed Envelope Model Predictive Control for Autonomous Racing
authors: Y. Guo; H. Gan; S. Yu; C. Shen; T. Ersal
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Raceline-Informed Envelope-Based Model Predictive Control (RE-MPC) framework for autonomous racing that pushes the vehicle to its dynamic limits through real-time planning while accounting for an online-generated geometric raceline. Prior work has shown that Envelope-Based Model Predictive Control (E-MPC) can generate dynamically feasible and collision-free racing trajectories without relying on a predefined reference path. However, its local planning nature may result in suboptimal behavior in complex scenarios. To mitigate this shortcoming of E-MPC, the new RE-MPC framework incorporates a reference raceline into the optimization process. The approach consists of two steps. First, similar to the state of the art, the drivable region for each track is segmented into a sequence of blocks that collectively form an envelope, ensuring that the vehicle remains within track boundaries. The second step marks the original contribution of this paper by generating a geometric raceline online and applying additional costs on selective prediction horizon points along the raceline rather than strictly adhering to it. The RE-MPC framework is evaluated and validated in simulation across various race tracks for autonomous racing. The results demonstrate that RE-MPC improves racing performance over the state of the art on all the tracks tested while maintaining real-time computational performance. These results indicate the potential of the RE-MPC approach to provide performant, robust, and real-time feasible optimization solutions for autonomous racing in diverse scenarios.

title: VERIFIX-BI: Deterministic Constrained Repair for Business-Intelligence Packages
authors: K. Elansari
abstract: BI assistants generate packages combining SQL, metrics, charts, filters, links, and evidence. We present VERIFIX-BI, a deterministic constrained repair method that sanitizes runtime inputs, enumerates finite typed candidates, applies package-level hard validation, ranks feasible candidates conservatively, and abstains when a detected defect or evidence risk has no safe supported repair. Clean-room separation excludes evaluation-only fields and prior repair outputs from candidate generation and selection. Across four main suites, VERIFIX-BI accepts 7,037 repairs among 17,100 cases: 103/330 Core hidden failures, 1,179/1,600 Broad hidden failures, 5,628/8,000 Corruption Stress cases, and 127/165 Public Executable hidden failures. The Public result comprises 27/65 BIRD defects and 100/100 nvBench defects; Spider contributes valid controls only. Core also exposes a selectivity cost: VERIFIX-BI conservatively abstains on 73/170 valid packages (42.9%). No harmful edit to a valid input, applicable-witness failure among accepted repairs, or leakage failure was observed. Post-run hidden-reference agreement was 102/103 for Core and complete for the accepted Broad, Corruption Stress, and Public repairs under exact, projection-equivalent, or dialect-equivalent comparison. On 24 defective Tableau packages, VERIFIX-BI exactly repaired 17 and partially repaired 1; none of 16 valid packages was modified. On 1,500 poisoned-evidence cases, disabling evidence-risk abstention left repair count unchanged at 235 but allowed 374/375 unresolved risky cases to pass through unchanged. On a fixed 600-case Qwen2.5-Coder-7B comparison, raw model output harmfully modified 234/267 valid inputs, whereas both gated conditions recorded zero harmful valid-input edits. These results characterize a validator-relative coverage–safety tradeoff within the implemented typed grammar.

title: A Decision-Aware Machine Learning Framework for Reliable Breast Cancer Classification
authors: A. Kalita; H. Kalita; K. Das
venue: 2026 International Conference on Innovative Trends in Information Technology (ICITIIT)
abstract: Machine learning models have demonstrated strong performance in breast cancer classification; however, most existing approaches rely on forced predictions for all samples, which can be risky in safety-critical clinical settings [6]. In practice, misclassification of ambiguous cases may lead to severe consequences, particularly in automated decision-support systems [7]. This paper presents a decision-aware machine learning framework that increases prediction reliability by integrating confidence-based abstention into the classification process. The proposed framework allows the model to defer decisions when predictive confidence falls within an uncertain range, thereby reducing the risk of erroneous predictions. Logistic Regression and Random Forest classifiers are evaluated on the Breast Cancer Wisconsin dataset [1] using a strict train-validation-test protocol. Experimental results show that while baseline models achieve high overall accuracy, the decision-aware framework eliminates misclassifications on high-confidence cases at the cost of reduced coverage. On the test set, the framework achieves perfect accuracy on decided samples while abstaining from a small fraction of ambiguous cases. These findings demonstrate that confidence-aware decision policies can improve the reliability of machine learning systems for clinical decision support without modifying the underlying classifier.

title: Confidence-Calibrated Caformer-S18 for Reliable Malabar Spinach Disease Recognition Under Class Imbalance
authors: E. Jain
venue: 2026 7th International Conference on Smart Electronics and Communication (ICOSEC)
abstract: Automated plant disease recognition is useful for early crop monitoring, but practical deployment requires more than high classification accuracy. A model should also be able to give a good confidence estimate, allowing cases of uncertain or visual ambiguity to be deferred for expert review. In this paper, a reliability-aware CaFormer-S18 framework is proposed for Malabar spinach disease recognition under a highly imbalanced dataset setting. The study is based on the Malabar Spinach Disease Detection Dataset, which has five classes: Anthracnose, Bacterial-Spot, Downy-Mildew, Healthy-Leaf, and Pest-Damage. No customized enhancement or extra attention modules were used, and a basic preprocessing pipeline was used, involving resizing and normalization. The CaFormer-S18 model was evaluated using accuracy, macro-F1, weighted-F1, balanced accuracy, Cohen's kappa, Matthews correlation coefficient, calibration behavior, residual error topology, and selective prediction analysis. The model was evaluated on the held-out test set, and its accuracy, macro-F1, weighted-F1, and balanced accuracy were 82.26%, 79.36%, 82.10%, and 81.06%, respectively. The calibration error of the model was reasonably aligned, with an expected calibration error of 0.068. The classes of visually overlapping Pest-Damage, Healthy-Leaf, and Bacterial-Spot had the majority of the residual errors. The results indicate that CaFormer-S18 can be used for reliability-aware agricultural decision-making when used with confidence-based accept-or-defer prediction.

title: HGT-PPO: A Hybrid Graph-Transformer Approach for Large-Scale DAG Task Scheduling in SAGIN
authors: M. Chen; J. Liu; Q. Xiu; J. Qu
abstract: Space–air–ground integrated network (SAGIN) provides a promising computing infrastructure for 6G applications, but scheduling large-scale directed acyclic graph (DAG) tasks in such networks remains challenging due to dynamic topology, heterogeneous resources, and complex intertask dependencies. This article investigates DAG task scheduling in SAGIN with the objective of minimizing the weighted cost of completion delay and energy consumption. To address the exponential action-space growth caused by large DAGs, we propose a dynamic task execution window (DTEW)-enabled hybrid graph-transformer (HGT)-proximal policy optimization (PPO) framework. DTEW dynamically constructs the executable task window at each decision epoch according to DAG dependency constraints and real-time resource feasibility, while incorporating bounded deferral and automatic retry strategies to improve scheduling flexibility and fault tolerance. Unlike prior graph neural network (GNN)-based schedulers that capture only explicit serial dependencies along DAG edges, the HGT-PPO architecture further models the latent contention structure among parallelizable subtasks within each execution window and the cross-domain alignment between task requirements and heterogeneous server capabilities, enabling a more comprehensive state representation for policy learning. Extensive experiments under varying DAG scales, server configurations, and network volatility conditions demonstrate that HGT-PPO consistently outperforms existing methods in total cost, task completion rate, and robustness.

title: Dynamic State-Aware Channel Selection for IEEE 802.11bn Non-Primary Channel Access
authors: T. -H. Lin; W. -D. Shen; H. -Y. Wei
venue: 2026 IEEE VTS Asia Pacific Wireless Communications Symposium (APWCS)
abstract: The evolution of wireless local area networks (WLANs) toward the IEEE 802.11bn standard (Wi-Fi 8) indicates a shift from prioritizing peak physical-layer throughput to achieving Ultra-High Reliability (UHR). As Wi-Fi standards expand channel bandwidths, the medium access control (MAC) architecture remains constrained by the primary channel bottleneck. Under the Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance (CSMA/CA) protocol, when the primary channel is occupied by an Overlapping Basic Service Set (OBSS), devices enter a deferral state, leading to spectrum underutilization across secondary channels. To address this issue, the IEEE 802.11 UHR task group introduced the Non-Primary Channel Access (NPCA) mechanism. However, the current standard draft restricts each BSS to a static, single Non-Primary Channel (NPCH), making the network vulnerable to secondary channel congestion. This paper investigates the limitations of the single-anchor NPCA protocol and proposes a Dynamic Multi-NPCH Selection architecture to improve overall channel access efficiency. By relaxing the constraint of the NPCA transmission from a fixed secondary anchor, our framework introduces three schemes: Static Single-NPCH Selection (SSNS), Periodic Randomized NPCH Selection (PRNS), and Dynamic State-Aware NPCH Selection (DSANS). The proposed architectures allow the BSS to evaluate spectral conditions and select a suitable available channel, thereby enhancing spectrum utilization and reducing latency in dense deployment scenarios.

title: Zero-Misprint Asset Identification and Risk Control Method for Industrial Environments
authors: Y. Shen; T. Wang; F. Tan
venue: 2025 7th International Academic Exchange Conference on Science and Technology Innovation (IAECST)
abstract: In industrial production environments, printer operations within production networks are subject to stringent constraints imposed by production processes. Due to the distinctive characteristics of printer protocols, traditional port scanning and fingerprinting methods are prone to triggering spurious printing or service disruptions, potentially leading to production incidents. This paper proposes a three-tier adaptive identification framework integrating lightweight fingerprinting, behavioral profiling, and machine learning, coupled with read-only security plugins and auditable decision pathways. In production environments encompassing more than 3,000 devices (including 500+ printers) and control settings, the framework achieves a misidentification rate below 0.3% while maintaining zero spurious printing, and constrains the update latency for vulnerable assets within 300 seconds. Furthermore, we introduce a selective identification mechanism with conservative abstention based on conformal prediction, whichsafely handles boundary samples at confidence level 1−α, demonstrating the feasibility of mitigating risks associated with deep protocol interactions.

title: CodeFit. Investigating the Impact of Providing Free Access to Campus Sports Facilities on the Mental Health and Academic Outcomes of Postgraduate Software Engineering Students
authors: A. McGowan; N. Anderson; L. Galway
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of providing free access to campus sports facilities on the mental health, physical fitness, lifestyle activities and academic outcomes of postgraduate students pursuing a Computer Masters degree at a UK University. Utilising controlled barrier access tracking to campus sport facilities and periodic surveys, data was collected to examine changes in mental health indicators, physical activity levels, and social interactions throughout the academic year. Results reveal a complex interplay between access to sports facilities, mental well-being, and academic performance. While there is an increase in mental health issues during the course, the utilisation of sports facilities correlates with reduced Exceptional Circumstance requests (application for an extension to a coursework deadline or exam deferral) related to stress and anxiety. Additionally, increased attendance and engagement in the course were recorded, as was marginally better academic outcomes. However, students that stated they had frequent mental health concerns statistically performed worse in assessments. Furthermore, while there was a concerning increase in mental health issues among students during the course, there was a decrease in other reported external stressors such as body image, physical health, and loneliness. It is significant that the frequency of students feeling regularly concerned about their mental health in this study was 41%, which compares favorably with the comparative university average of 79%. The findings underscore the importance of providing students with access to physical activity resources and support systems to enhance overall well-being and academic success. Further research is needed to optimise student support mechanisms and promote holistic student development within the university context.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Pneumonia Screening from Chest X-Rays Using Selective Triage and Explainable Deep Learning
authors: S. R. V. S; P. Shetty; M. S. N; S. Kini
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Emerging Synergy Science and Technology (ICESST)
abstract: Pneumonia remains a major global health concern, requiring timely and reliable diagnostic support, particularly in settings with limited access to expert radiological interpretation. Although deep learning models applied to chest X-ray (CXR) imaging have demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy, their clinical deployment is constrained by predictive overconfidence, limited calibration, and the absence of mechanisms to safely defer uncertain decisions. Addressing these challenges, this study presents a confidence-aware pneumonia screening framework based exclusively on chest X-ray images. The proposed approach employs a lightweight convolutional neural network built on MobileNetV2 using transfer learning to classify chest X-rays into normal and pneumonia categories. Beyond conventional performance evaluation, the framework explicitly incorporates predictive confidence to enable selective triage, allowing the model to automatically accept high-confidence predictions while escalating low-confidence cases for human review. Model reliability is assessed through calibration analysis using Expected Calibration Error (ECE), and clinical interpretability is supported via Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM), which highlights salient radiographic regions influencing predictions. Experimental results demonstrate strong discriminative performance (AUC-ROC 0.96) while enabling meaningful trade-offs between automation coverage and diagnostic risk. The findings indicate that uncertainty-aware selective screening can improve the safety, transparency, and trustworthiness of deep learning-based medical imaging systems. The framework is positioned as a practical decision-support tool and provides a foundation for future research toward extended and multimodal diagnostic workflows.

title: Abstaining ECG Classifiers Through Explainable Prototypical Spaces
authors: S. Dakshit
venue: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Healthcare Informatics (ICHI)
abstract: Deep learning models have been deployed for var-ious healthcare tasks owing to their success in ingesting dif-ferent modalities of raw multimedia data. Despite the recent advancements, their widespread adoption in the critical domain of healthcare is restricted due to lack of trust in black-box models. Furthermore, the shortcomings of the existing popu-lar evaluation metrics neither incites confidence in the model predictions nor quantifies model performance capacity towards responsibility for incorrect decisions. In this paper, we propose an abstention method for Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models by quantification of the embedding space of the networks as prototypical space for each class to explain model capacity, improve performance through responsibility. The prototypical space for each class is the most confident space where the samples are correctly classified with minimal error consequently improving confidence and reliability in the model predictions. We demonstrate improvement in performance up to 18.17% and 12.10% through abstention of model outcomes by identification of outcomes which can be confidently trusted based on the prototypical spaces for each class and network architecture invariance of our proposed approach with two different 2D CNN architectures on the public MIT-BIH ECG dataset. The improvement in performance through our explainable abstaining method mitigates risk in crucial healthcare tasks and improves reliability in model predictions. We also discuss future improvements and applications of our proposed prototypical spaces in the domain of healthcare.

title: Confidence Estimation via Auxiliary Models
authors: C. Corbière; N. Thome; A. Saporta; T. -H. Vu; M. Cord; P. Pérez
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Reliably quantifying the confidence of deep neural classifiers is a challenging yet fundamental requirement for deploying such models in safety-critical applications. In this paper, we introduce a novel target criterion for model confidence, namely the true class probability (TCP). We show that TCP offers better properties for confidence estimation than standard maximum class probability (MCP). Since the true class is by essence unknown at test time, we propose to learn TCP criterion from data with an auxiliary model, introducing a specific learning scheme adapted to this context. We evaluate our approach on the task of failure prediction and of self-training with pseudo-labels for domain adaptation, which both necessitate effective confidence estimates. Extensive experiments are conducted for validating the relevance of the proposed approach in each task. We study various network architectures and experiment with small and large datasets for image classification and semantic segmentation. In every tested benchmark, our approach outperforms strong baselines.

title: The Next Paradigm in Medical AI: A Survey of Agentic AI in Biomedicine
authors: A. Abdollahi; M. A. Rezaei; X. Wang; D. Cai; S. He; S. M. Ayyoubzadeh; Y. Nie; H. Chen
abstract: Biomedical AI is increasingly shaped by policy-bound, multi-step clinical workflows and non-stationary, multimodal data and tools. In this setting, the field is moving beyond static predictors toward agentic systems, enabled by foundation models that maintain task-relevant state and operate through a closed perceive$\rightarrow$plan$\rightarrow$act$\rightarrow$observe loop under explicit oversight. However, the field lacks a coherent account that defines biomedical agency, relates foundational model capabilities to agent behaviors, and traces the pathway from pretraining to domain-adapted, deployable systems. This survey offers such an account by synthesizing operational boundaries of agency and framing six core components (memory, planning, reflection, tool use, dialogue, and collaboration) as foundational agent-enabling capabilities that drive the transition from isolated pipelines to fully realized agents. This survey situates these perspectives along the model-building pathway, from pretraining through post-training adaptation to the orchestration mechanisms that operationalize agents. We highlight safety and governance considerations for high-stakes settings, emphasizing the fidelity of process and reasoning, uncertainty and abstention, privacy and provenance, and human oversight. Taken together, this survey provides a structured synthesis of how recent work connects foundation models to governable biomedical agentic systems and distills the recurring challenges and directions identified in the literature for reliable, accountable deployment.

title: From Satellite to UAV Imagery: Calibration and Collapse-Aware Triage for Trustworthy Post-Earthquake Building Damage Assessment
authors: M. E. Soyhan; K. Elgazzar
venue: 2026 11th International Conference on Computer Science and Engineering (UBMK)
abstract: Deep neural networks trained on satellite imagery for post-disaster building damage assessment are increasingly considered for deployment on uncrewed aerial vehicle imagery, where rapid local response is needed. This paper shows that such transfer is unsafe in a specific and measurable way: a satellite-trained classifier applied to post-earthquake aerial imagery is not only inaccurate but confidently wrong, and its confident errors concentrate on the collapsed-building class that matters most for life safety. Because labeled aerial earthquake data is scarce, the paper studies trustworthiness rather than retraining. A spectrum of label-aware and label-free interventions is evaluated on two independent aerial targets, a Türkiye 2023 earthquake dataset and the Hurricane Michael RescueNet dataset, across two convolutional backbones and one vision transformer. Target-domain temperature scaling reduces calibration error from above 0.22 to below 0.11 without changing accuracy, while source-domain scaling fails. Label-free test-time adaptation degrades both accuracy and calibration and merely shifts the model’s bias rather than correcting it. A small amount of labeled target data, adapted with linear probing followed by fine-tuning, recovers accuracy with as few as twenty patches per class and calibration by forty. When no labels are available, a collapse-aware triage that ranks buildings by predicted collapse risk reduces missed collapsed structures for a given amount of human review. This paper reports the inference cost of each option, showing that the trustworthiness layer runs at negligible inference cost while test-time adaptation is expensive. The findings replicate across both aerial targets, supporting a practical recipe for trustworthy cross-domain deployment.

title: Hidden-Uncertainty Assessment via Non-Verbalized Signatures for LLM Medical QA
authors: E. D'Urso
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown growing potential in medical applications, yet reliable uncertainty estimation remains a key safety bottleneck in medical QA. Reasoning-capable models can still produce incorrect answers with high confidence, both when confidence is self-reported and when inferred from answer-probability proxies (answer log-probabilities/option-softmax). While self-consistency can improve reliability, it requires multiple forward passes and is costly at inference time. We propose a lightweight Trust–Abstain supervised classifier that predicts error risk from a single reasoning trace, shifting attention from answer tokens to the reasoning process by combining trace-level log-probability dynamics, textual markers, and medical-domain signals. We evaluate five open-weight reasoning LLMs, including GPT-oss-120B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-32B, across ten medical benchmarks ( $N=21{,}324$ ) under a Leave-One-Dataset-Out protocol. Our approach improves ROC–AUC by 2.4–6.0 points over strong single-pass baselines, including self-verbalized confidence and answer-probability proxies. In selective answering regimes (10–40% coverage), it reduces absolute error rate by up to 9.7 percentage points and consistently increases Accuracy–Coverage AUC. A simple logistic regression matches non-linear alternatives. Finally, we identify 12 generalizable features that remain stable across model families. Freezing the feature space to these predictors incurs a small degradation (mean <1%) relative to model-specific selection, supporting largely model-agnostic uncertainty signals. We release code, datasets, and demos to support reproducibility.

title: Causal Edge Intelligence with Counterfactual Reasoning for Gut Microbiota-Informed Intracranial Aneurysm Rupture-Risk Assessment in Autonomous Healthcare IoT Systems
authors: C. Huang; A. Li; R. Zhu; M. A. Alohali; H. Elmannai; F. Duan; B. Luo; Z. Peng; D. Kang
abstract: Autonomous healthcare Internet of Things (IoT) systems require accurate predictions and reliable decisions regarding sensing, communication, and computation under changing patient conditions, data quality, and resource conditions. This study proposes MICRO-CARE, a dual-timescale causal patient-edge digital twin framework for gut microbiota-informed intracranial aneurysm rupture risk assessment and counterfactual autonomous Internet-of-Things control. MICRO-CARE couples time-unrolled biological and IoT structural causal models with quality-aware graph-constrained multimodal fusion, longitudinal competing risk inference, calibrated/conformal uncertainty, out-of-distribution detection, and safety-constrained counterfactual action selection. Autonomous actions are restricted to sensing, modality activation, packet prioritization, execution placement, repeated measurements, abstention, and clinician escalation. In external-center validation, MICRO-CARE achieved a time-dependent concordance index of 0.809 (95% CI: 0.785-0.831), compared with 0.752 (0.726-0.776) for the strongest non-causal multimodal comparator, with an integrated Brier score of 0.072 (0.065-0.079). Across 312 controlled IoT intervention episodes, counterfactual predictions achieved R2 values of 0.74-0.81 for uncertainty and latency and 0.68-0.76 for energy and alert reliability effects. Under network congestion, the P99 end-to-end latency was 1.18 s with 98.6% delivery reliability, whereas the prescribed latency-reliability service-level objective was maintained through at least 100 concurrent streams. These results demonstrate the intervention-aware, uncertainty-aware, and safety-bounded causal edge intelligence for autonomous healthcare IoT.

title: Machine Learning for Modern Cybersecurity: Trend-Driven Architectures, Threat Models, and Quantitative Evaluation
authors: N. S. Vummaneni; I. Kumar; A. Mittal; S. Bharadwaj; H. Varshney
abstract: Machine learning (ML) has become a default substrate for contemporary cybersecurity—from network intrusion detection and malware classification to phishing defense and security analytics over cloud telemetry. At the same time, cybersecurity is now a first-class stress test for ML: adversaries actively manipulate inputs, labels, data pipelines, and even model supply chains. Recent trends amplify both promise and risk: transformer backbones that learn directly from raw traffic or byte streams; self-supervised pretraining over petabyte-scale logs; federated and privacy-preserving learning at the network edge; and agentic large language model (LLM) copilots that triage incidents and generate remediation steps. This paper presents a complete, quantitative research study of ML-for-cybersecurity under these trends. We propose a threat-aware end-to-end pipeline, GuardML, that integrates (i) representation learning for heterogeneous security signals, (ii) robustness layers against evasion/poisoning/extraction, and (iii) operational guardrails for deployment (calibration, abstention, provenance-aware retrieval for RAG). We develop reproducible experimental methodology and stage-wise energy/latency models, then evaluate on a curated multi-domain benchmark protocol (TRISHIELD) spanning network intrusion, malware, and phishing. Across tasks, a trendaligned transformer stack achieves macro-F1 scores of 0.91 for NIDS, 0.94 for malware, and 0.95 for phishing, representing improvements of 4–11 points over gradient-boosted decision tree baselines. Under adversarial evasion, our guardrail-enhanced models maintain true positive rates of 0.91 at 0.1% false positive rate for NIDS compared to 0.71 for undefended baselines. We show that lightweight, composable guardrails reduce attack success rates by 32–61% with only 7–9% latency overhead, and we derive five actionable design rules linking model choice, feature exposure, and security posture.

title: CANDLE: Connectivity-Aware Semantic Delegation for Energy-Budgeted Agent Reasoning in Intermittently Connected Vehicular Networks
authors: M. Ali; T. Qayyum; Z. Trabelsi
venue: IEEE Open Journal of Vehicular Technology
abstract: Autonomous agents deployed on vehicles and mobile IoT devices promise to reduce edge and cloud load, but they reason under a regime that existing offloading frameworks do not capture: connectivity that appears and disappears on the timescale of a single multi-step task, and on-device inference whose energy cost exceeds a sustainable power budget. We argue that in this regime the agent must decide not only where to reason, but what to communicate and when. We present CANDLE, a framework in which the unit of offloading is an agent reasoning step with an adjustable semantic fidelity, and placement (local, V2V peer, edge, cloud, or deferral) is chosen jointly with fidelity by a training-free online controller derived via Lyapunov drift-plus-penalty optimization. CANDLE attains a utility within $O(1/V)$ of the optimum achievable by any causal policy while provably meeting per-node average power budgets, and we show that the guarantee degrades gracefully linearly in the error of the connectivity predictor it uses. We further show that the per-node minimization remains an exact minimizer of the drift-plus-penalty bound under realized, shared-resource contention (RSU compute/bandwidth and V2V peer compute), that accounting for payload-dependent prefill compute changes the fidelity/placement tradeoff without changing this conclusion, and that a hard-budget-gated heuristic and a policy whose weights are learned rather than derived remain dominated by CANDLE. A disruption-tolerant messaging protocol based on resumable custody tokens allows in-flight reasoning steps to survive coverage gaps and RSU handovers. In a reproducible vehicular simulation with heterogeneous onboard compute, including a mobility scenario whose speed, dwell, and turning statistics are calibrated from a real public urban taxi-GPS trace, CANDLE is the only competitive policy that respects a 3 W average power budget, including against an energy-budget-gated heuristic and policies whose weights are learned rather than derived: it delivers, at the reference density, higher completion than the strongest unconstrained baseline (Myopic-Latency) at 52% of its energy and $1.9\times$ its utility per joule, and overtakes it in absolute completion once roadside coverage reaches 50% or above, a regime in which it also remains competitive under a second, real-trace-calibrated mobility scenario.

title: A Multi-Agent Reasoning Reliability Framework for Autonomous Decision Support and Its Preliminary Evaluation on StrategyQA
authors: E. Ezin
venue: 2026 34th Signal Processing and Communications Applications Conference (SIU)
abstract: High accuracy alone is not sufficient in autonomous decision support; the underlying reasoning must also be reliable, explainable, and auditable. This study proposes a safety-oriented auditing framework combining multi-agent reasoning, Theory-of-Mind-based critique, and symbolic verification, and presents a preliminary evaluation on the StrategyQA dataset. StrategyQA is utilized as a structural proxy for the multi-step reasoning processes involved in autonomous network control decisions. In the framework, an agent produces an answer and rationale, a critic agent questions hidden beliefs and conflicting assumptions, and a symbolic verifier checks logical consistency before the final decision. This structure enables measurable and reproducible evaluation of safety-oriented decision support. In experiments on 100 samples, the full pipeline achieved the highest accepted accuracy of 0.96, with an abstention rate of 0.50.

title: Achievable Error Exponents for Almost Fixed-Length M-ary Classification
authors: J. Diao; L. Zhou; L. Bai
venue: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory (ISIT)
abstract: We revisit the multiple classification problem and propose a two-phase test, where each phase is a fixed-length test and the second-phase proceeds only if a reject option is decided in the first phase. We derive the achievable error exponent under each hypothesis and show that our two-phase test bridges over the fixed-length test of Gutman (TIT, 1989) and the sequential test of Haghifam, Tan, and Khisti (TIT 2021). In contrast to the fixed-length test of Gutman that requires an additional reject option, with proper choices of test parameters, our test achieves error exponents close to the sequential test of Haghifam, Tan, and Khisti without a reject option. We generalize the result of Lalitha and Javidi (ISIT 2016) for binary hypothesis testing to the more practical families of M-ary statistical classification, where the test outcome is more than two and the generating distribution under each hypothesis is unknown.

title: Small-Sample Tail Latency Prediction for Cloud Time-Series Database Services via Censoring-Aware Extreme Value Theory
authors: F. Fu
venue: 2026 IEEE 19th International Conference on Cloud Computing (CLOUD)
abstract: Cloud services with query timeouts produce right-censored latency data: the most extreme observations—precisely those that determine tail risk—are hidden behind the timeout boundary. We frame this as a problem of safe deployment screening under unavoidable censoring, not a general solution to small-sample tail prediction. We show that timeout-induced censoring causes every standard tail-latency estimator to miss 100% of true service-level objective (SLO) violations in screening, creating a dangerous blind spot for capacity planning. We present CenEVT, which treats timed-out queries as censored evidence rather than discarding them, fitting a penalized Generalized Pareto Distribution (GPD) via censored maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) to predict the 99th-percentile (p99) latency from small pilot samples (50–200 queries). A confidence-interval (CI) based decision rule, augmented with a regime-gated abstention for extreme censoring, flags SLO risk when uncertainty warrants caution. Evaluated on 618,660 experiment rows from two TSDB engines (TimescaleDB, ClickHouse) across six query templates, CenEVT detects 99.9% of true violations (0.06% false-safe rate) where all censoring-blind baselines miss 100%, with a quantile score (QS) 6.7× lower than naive methods. Against the strongest censored parametric baselines (log-normal, Weibull) the gap is operational: across the corpus CenEVT misses 27 fewer true SLO violations than censored log-normal, the gap ×concentrated in the subtle regime (low timeout rate, tight SLO). The censoring problem we identify is not specific to TSDBs—it affects any cloud service where requests are killed at a deadline.

title: Hybrid Energy Storage System Optimization With Battery Charging and Swapping Coordination
authors: X. Chen; Y. Yang; J. Song; J. Wang; G. He
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Battery storage is a key technology for distributed renewable energy integration. Wider applications of battery storage systems call for smarter and more flexible deployment models to improve their economic viability. Here we propose a hybrid energy storage system (HESS) model that flexibly coordinates both portable energy storage systems (PESSs) and stationary energy storage systems (SESSs) in a grid. PESSs are batteries and power conversion systems loaded on vehicles that travel between grid nodes with price differences to alleviate grid congestion. PESSs can charge/discharge at grid nodes or swap (part of) batteries with SESSs for profit maximization. We introduce a spatiotemporal decision-making framework for HESS including the planning of SESS and the on- demand dispatch of PESS. We propose a two-phase decision-making algorithm (TPDM), where the first phase uses a spatiotemporal cost-effectiveness aggregation method to determine the optimal SESS location; the second phase shapes a low-complexity solution space by arc destroying and repairing. The results show that HESS achieves significant arbitrage benefit improvement in 86.3% of the operating periods through a year compared with SESS and PESS alone. Compared with commercial solver, the proposed TPDM, on average, can reduce the computational time by 95.5% with an optimality of 1.04%. Note to Practitioners—Battery storage and electric vehicles (EVs) play a crucial role in renewable energy integration and in shaping a low-carbon and sustainable energy and transportation systems. To achieve efficient and scalable management of battery storage across energy and transportation systems, we incorporate the portable energy storage (i.e., batteries transported by vehicles) and stationary energy storage (i.e., batteries placed at grids), into a hybrid energy storage system (HESS), and develop efficient planning framework and scheduling algorithms. Specifically, the proposed methods can provide decision supports for the owners of battery assets to determine the optimal SESS location and for the high-quality coordination of battery charging, swapping, and routing in a HESS. Our methods also have potentials in the on- demand applications of battery storage and EVs across energy and transportation systems, such as ancillary services, grid investment deferral, and battery trading and sharing.

title: Trustworthy Explainable AI for Cross-Dataset Brain Tumor Diagnosis from MRI
authors: K. Manjusha; K. Nagaraju; P. H. Priya; M. Sumalatha; K. Tejaswini; P. Sreeshma
venue: 2026 9th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Control Systems (ICICCS)
abstract: Diagnosing brain tumors through magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is of great importance, correctly and reliably because of the domain shift, uncertainty in the models, and even because of insufficient interpretation of automated systems. In this paper, an integrated credible and explicable framework of artificial intelligence aimed at incorporating tumor-sensitive representation learning, exposition-steadfast feature selection, uncertainty-senient classification, and selective prediction coupled with probability modification, to aid sound clinical decision representation, is presented. On a cross-dataset evaluation protocol, which trains the models using the Figshare Brain Tumor Dataset and test them using the BraTS MRI Dataset, the proposed framework shows an accuracy of 92.37% and area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.948, with substantially better calibration reliability, with an expected calibration error of 0.031, in comparison to hybrid, convolutional, and transformer baselines. Quantitative explainability tests show more faithfulness (0.74) and stability (0.81) scores compared to other competing methods. Reliability maps and visualization illustrations also show consistent estimates of confidence and attention of the models focused on the lesions. These findings support the fact that the framework is always improving the predictive performance, calibration reliability, and the explanation quality across architectures. The future research will broaden the assessment to bigger multi-centric studies on clinical cohorts, study semi-supervised pretraining techniques, in addition to causal interpretability using human-in-the-loop mechanisms to enhance further the bridge between automated reasoning and expert clinical delineations.

title: UL-GSR: Uncertainty-Aware Scenario Recognition for Low-Cost GNSS Sensors in Urban Environments
authors: H. Shen; H. Liu; Y. Wang; B. Wei; X. Fan; C. Qian
venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Scenario-adaptive positioning for low-cost global navigation satellite system (GNSS) terminals requires accurate urban scenario recognition together with reliable estimates of predictive confidence. An uncertainty-aware urban scenario recognition framework, termed UL-GSR, is proposed by integrating dual uncertainty modeling with selective prediction correction. RGB Voronoi images jointly encode satellite geometry, carrier-to-noise density ratio (C/N0), pseudorange multipath residuals, and loss-of-lock indicator (LLI). Aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty are modeled using heteroscedastic Gaussian logits and Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout, respectively, and the resulting predictive entropy is used to selectively trigger deterministic correction and causal probability fusion for highly uncertain epochs. Eight-fold grouped cross-validation was conducted on 18,000 epochs collected in Luohu District, Shenzhen, covering five urban scenarios. UL-GSR achieved an accuracy of (88.22%± 4.59%) and a macro F1-score of (87.22% ± 4.25%), yielding the highest mean performance among all evaluated models, with statistically significant improvements over the baseline CNN. UL-GSR also achieved the lowest expected calibration error, negative log-likelihood, and Brier score among all comparison models. The predictive-entropy gate forwarded only 30.57% of the test epochs to the correction stage while covering 77.04% of the first-stage classification errors, ultimately improving the final accuracy by 4.84 percentage points over the first-stage output.
