It also obtained the lowest Brier score of 0.146 and negative log-likelihood of 0.425, although Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization achieved a marginally lower expected calibration error. Confidence-based deferral increased selective weighted F1 to 85.31% while retaining 84.8% of predictions. Under controlled modality masking, MSA-DBO achieved the highest weighted F1 under each single-modality omission, whereas BOHB performed slightly better when two modalities were simultaneously unavailable and retained an advantage in search efficiency. Overall, the results indicate that MSA-DBO provides a reliability-oriented hyperparameter-search strategy under the present controlled MELD-derived feature-level conditions. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Detection of AI-Generated Source Code in Programming Assignments
authors: Vysocan, Jakub; Bubenkova, Lenka; Pietrikova, Emilia
venue: INES 2026 - 2026 IEEE 30th Jubilee International Conference on Intelligent Engineering Systems, Proceedings
abstract: The widespread adoption of large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT and Gemini has raised concerns about academic integrity in programming courses. Students can use these tools to generate complete assignment solutions, yet traditional plagiarism detectors fail to identify AI-generated code because LLMs produce non-deterministic, syntactically diverse outputs. This paper presents a machine-learning-based approach for distinguishing AI-generated C source code from student-written code. We construct a labeled dataset of 16,271 samples (8,782 AI-generated across five LLM families and 7,489 verified student solutions from two historical student cohorts (2021 pre-ChatGPT and 2022 proxy-verified as low-contamination)) and evaluate TF-IDF character n-gram classifiers under multiple data-splitting strategies designed to test generalization. Our best model achieves near-ceiling in-distribution performance (macro-F1 = 0.998 on by-student split) but reveals significant limitations under out-of-distribution conditions, including severe degradation on unseen assignment types and increasing AI-like classification rates on newer student cohorts whose true authorship is uncertain. We argue that such detectors are best deployed as risk-ranking support tools rather than standalone enforcement mechanisms, requiring calibration, abstention thresholds, and human review in practice. © 2026 IEEE.

title: ProSyn-Net: A Reliable Prototypical Synergy Network for Imbalanced Dermatologic Multimodal Ultrasound Diagnosis
authors: Lin, Jicheng; Dai, Xiangning; Wang, Beidi; Feng, Juncai; Liu, Haotian; Yu, Chenke; Liu, Ruimeng; Qin, Ziwei; Zhao, Yujing; Luo, Ye
abstract: Multimodal ultrasound, combining B-mode and color Doppler, is vital for the early screening of skin lesions. However, its automated clinical application is severely hindered by modality quality disparities, incidence-driven data imbalance, and model over-confidence. To this end, we propose ProSyn-Net, a unified multimodal diagnostic framework comprising three synergistic modules. First, a dynamic cross-attention fusion module adaptively aligns morphological and hemodynamic features while suppressing modality noise. The fused representations are then processed by a non-linear prototypical mapping module, which effectively disentangles complex, non-convex minority samples from majority clusters in a high-dimensional space. Finally, an uncertainty-aware manifold ensemble leverages the geometric diversity of these prototypes to yield reliable predictions and extract predictive uncertainty. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ProSyn-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance on the primary in-house imbalanced 6-class dataset (78.60% Macro F1 and 96.66% AUC), while showing promising transferability on a complementary independent public binary dataset (87.80% accuracy). We further analyze uncertainty-guided selective deferral for ambiguous cases. Code is available at https://github.com/EdualcLin/ProSyn-Net. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Validation-calibrated Detector Banks for Ranked Attribution of Spatial Image Steganographic Algorithms
authors: Al-Saeedi, Hasan Karam; Hashim, Asaad Noori
venue: International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems
abstract: Spatial image steganalysis is commonly formulated as binary cover and stego detection under a known embedding algorithm and payload. Although this setting supports benchmarking, it is insufficient when a suspicious image is detected as steganographic but the embedding method remains unknown. This paper proposes a validation calibrated detector bank for ranked attribution of adaptive spatial image steganographic algorithms. Residual convolutional detectors are trained using leakage safe pair level splits. For each test image, frozen detectors produce a cross detector response vector, normalized with validation cover statistics and compared with validation response signatures. The framework returns ranked hypotheses, a candidate set, and a reject option for cover like inputs. Experiments on BOSSBase with five adaptive algorithms show that overlapping residual fingerprints limit exact Top 1 attribution. Nevertheless, the correct algorithm remains within the Top 3 hypotheses for 82.28 percent of stego images and the calibrated candidate set for 90.40 percent. This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/

title: Safe-by-Design Governance for LLM-Assisted Emergency Call Triage: Auditability, Human Oversight, and Degraded-Mode Resilience
authors: Guyeux, Christophe
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Smart Sustainable Systems for Computer and Engineering Applications, 3SCEA 2026
abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into Emergency Call Centers (112/911) promises to mitigate operator cognitive overload but introduces critical risks regarding hallucination, bias, and accountability. This paper presents 'secure-IAppel', a comprehensive Safe-by-Design governance framework for deploying AI assistance in life-critical environments. Moving beyond standard performance metrics (WER), we formalize governance as an architectural constraint and propose a hybrid pipeline combining a low-latency 'Hot Path' for realtime transcription with a verificational 'Cold Path' for safety auditing and retrospective corrections. In the IAppels project, this pipeline targets a unified emergency number (15/17/18/112) and operationalizes real-time STT (Whisper), language identification with translation, diarization, entity extraction, and AI-assisted decision trees for emergency call classification, under a subsecond latency budget. We define a rigorous 'Epistemic State Matrix' (Green/Orange/Red/Abstain) to manage algorithmic uncertainty, bound automation bias, and enforce effective Human-in-the-Loop oversight through explicit validation hooks. We further introduce standardized 'Reason Codes' that make abstentions and warnings auditable, and we link these logs to a privacyaware evidence chain compatible with GDPR and emerging AIact requirements. Finally, we show how explicit degraded modes preserve operational continuity under stress, ensuring that LLM assistance strengthens the human command chain rather than replacing it. The result is a governance-first blueprint grounded in the ongoing IAppels field experimentation (SDIS 01, 2025) that reconciles innovation with legal accountability and the ethical imperatives of public service. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Can We Predict LLM Reasoning Failures? Structural Predictability of Modal and Conditional Inference Errors
authors: Shahrokhshahi, Fatemeh; Mohammadi, Farzan
abstract: Large language models fail systematically on modal and conditional reasoning tasks, yet whether such failures are foreseeable remains unexplored. Selective prediction, the ability to abstain when a prediction is likely wrong, has been studied for factual NLP tasks but not for structured logical reasoning. We investigate whether LLM failures on seven modal and conditional inference patterns are predictable from the structural properties of reasoning problems, without relying on model outputs. Using 3,776 inference instances across nine models and three prompting strategies, we train an external classifier to predict per-instance failure from input-side features. Leave-one-pattern-out cross-validation reveals substantial variation in predictability: AUCROC ranges from 0.69 to 0.93, with patterns involving “must” operators being most predictable. We further show that targeted prompting (LogiCue), while reducing overall failures substantially, makes remaining failures structurally harder to predict. These findings suggest that input-side and output-side reliability mechanisms serve complementary roles in LLM reasoning pipelines. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: A Reliable Stream Learning Model for Network Intrusion Detection Systems
authors: Horchulhack, Pedro; Viegas, Eduardo Kugler; Santin, Altair Olivo
venue: Journal of the Brazilian Computer Society
abstract: Developing a reliable Network Intrusion Detection System (NIDS) remains a complex task due to the non-stationary nature of network traffic and the need for frequent updates to maintain high classification performance. Many existing approaches assume a stationary network environment, which overlooks the challenges associated with periodic model updates, such as the need for large amounts of properly labeled data and significant computational resources. This issue is particularly challenging for real-time applications, where minimizing delays and ensuring accuracy is crucial. This paper proposes an analysis of how changes in the network behavior negatively affects the long-term of ML-Based NIDS. For such a problem, it is proposed a new NIDS approach integrating stream learning with a reject option technique to simplify the model update process while ensuring consistent classification accuracy over time. The proposal uses stream learning classifiers to incrementally incorporate new data, while the reject option allows the system to evaluate the reliability of classifications before they are used for updates. The scheme operates with minimal intervention, with rejected instances stored for future updates and used to fine-tune the model over time, ensuring adaptation to evolving network conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach maintains high classification accuracy over a year, even without recurrent updates, and achieves significant improvements in true positive rates compared to traditional methods. The system can operate for up to three months without updates, with no significant degradation in performance. © 2026, Brazilian Computing Society. All rights reserved.

title: Governance-Aware Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Evidence Abstention for Reliable AI Policy Question Answering
authors: Jain, Ashish Hastimal; Yarrrabothu, Suhas Reddy; Kande, Nanda Kishore; Kethireddy, Dharmateja Reddy
venue: 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Systems, and Emerging Technologies, ICAISET 2026
abstract: Answering reliable questions over AI governance documents is still challenging since the traditional retrieval-augmented generation systems tend to provide responses that cannot be supported, do not differentiate between answerable questions and overly broad policy queries, and do not utilize governance indicators, including legal status, jurisdiction, and source authority. The paper introduces a governance-conscious agentic retrieval-augmented generation model with evidence abstinence to policy-sensitive question answering that answers only when the evidence retrieved is well-grounded and refers the cases of uncertainty to ABSTAIN / HUMAN REVIEW. It is based on the AGORA corpus of AI governance documents, retrieval of segments, a hybrid retriever that uses semantic similarity, lexical overlap and governance sensitive reranking, and a query risk layer of broad or globally framed queries. To preserve meaning of ground, the final answer module employs an extractive evidence-based composer rather than unconstrained generation. The proposed framework attained an almost perfect decision accuracy, 0.8583 mean retrieval keyword coverage on answerable queries, and 0.6833 mean answer keyword coverage with the selected extractive composer (0.5083) on a curated benchmark. These findings reveal a new and useful direction of the creation of reliable and policy-appropriate GenAI systems of the governance-seeking question answering. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Similarity-Aware Evaluation, Probability Calibration, and Independent Replication for Reliable Gastrointestinal Image Classification
authors: Liu, Housheng; Xu, Yingwu; Cheng, Fang; Zha, Jinlian
venue: International Journal of Imaging Systems and Technology
abstract: High accuracy alone does not establish reliable medical-image classification because visually similar images may cross partitions and confidence may be miscalibrated. We evaluated a similarity-aware framework on a four-class gastrointestinal benchmark (4000 images) and independently replicated the methodology on GastroVision (8000 images; 27 classes). A 64-bit DCT perceptual hash defined groups at Hamming distance ≤ 4. Five-fold random and group-constrained protocols were matched by model and seed, with separate validation, calibration, and test subsets. We compared modern backbones, temperature scaling, a 2 × 2 Mixup/label-smoothing ablation, and deterministic maximum-softmax probability. On the primary benchmark, grouped EfficientNet-B0 achieved accuracy and macro-F1 of 0.9765 ± 0.0022. Grouping changed accuracy by +0.0025 relative to random splitting (Wilcoxon p = 0.625). Temperature scaling reduced expected calibration error from 0.1292 ± 0.0216 to 0.0123 ± 0.0030 without changing predictions, and deterministic MSP achieved error-detection AUROC of 0.9288 ± 0.0181. On GastroVision, random folds contained 78–101 detected cross-subset overlaps, whereas grouped folds contained none. Grouped EfficientNet-B0 achieved 0.8195 ± 0.0043 accuracy and 0.5792 ± 0.0148 macro-F1; ECE decreased from 0.1114 ± 0.0148 to 0.0323 ± 0.0048 after scaling. Similarity grouping removed detected resemblance without reducing accuracy, while calibration and uncertainty analyses exposed properties hidden by discrimination metrics. GastroVision supports methodological portability rather than direct external validation; pHash cannot establish patient or procedure independence, for which identifiers remain preferable. © 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

title: 19th International Conference on Multi-disciplinary Trends in Artificial Intelligence, MIWAI 2026
abstract: The proceedings contain 38 papers. The special focus in this conference is on Multi-disciplinary Trends in Artificial Intelligence. The topics include: Detector Selection as a Network Science Problem: Accuracy-Scalability Trade-Offs in Distributed Edge Surveillance; multi-scale Visual Feature Extraction for Medical Visual Question Answering; calibration-Aware Lightweight Model Selection for Trustworthy Skin Lesion Classification; InjectGuard-RAG: Lightweight Defence Against Indirect Prompt Injection in Retrieval-Augmented Small-LLM Agents; title: Risk calibrated selective tabular transformers for explainable Alzheimer’s disease staging
authors: Ali, A. Nasreen; Madhu, K.P.
abstract: Background and objective: Early and reliable staging of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) using tabular clinical biomarkers is crucial but challenging due to heterogeneous features and model overconfidence. This research proposes a Risk-Calibrated Tabular Transformer (RC-TabFormer) that tokenises each feature, applies self-attention, employs temperature scaling for calibration, integrates a selective prediction mechanism that abstains on low-confidence cases, and fuses outputs with a LightGBM classifier. Methods: The research outcomes on Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) datasets with subject-level cross-validation, RC-TabFormer achieves 95.2 ± 0.5% accuracy, 96.7 ± 0.6% F1, 98.4 ± 0.4% AUC, 1.2 ± 0.2% Expected Calibration Error (ECE), and 91.2 ± 0.5% MCC for binary AD vs non-AD classification. On three-class Staging Alzheimer’s Disease, Mild Cognitive Impairment, Cognitively Normal (AD/CN/MCI) it attains 89.8 ± 0.5% accuracy, 89.7 ± 0.5% macro-F1, 95.1 ± 0.4% macro-AUC, 1.7 ± 0.3% ECE, and 84.3 ± 0.5% Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), surpassing strong baselines by up to 5 points while markedly improving calibration. Results: Coverage–risk curves show that selective prediction reduces errors at lower coverage, and explainability analyses using Integrated Gradients and SHAP identify key biomarkers such as Clinical Dementia Rating Scale Sum of Boxes (CDSRB) and tau (τ) ratios. RC-TabFormer provides a unified risk-aware framework that integrates Transformer-based tabular representation learning, LightGBM fusion, probability calibration, selective abstention, and feature-level explanation. The results demonstrate its potential for further external and prospective evaluation as a clinical decision-support framework. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Multi-Center validation of a Quality-Aware ordinal transformer for robust and Uncertainty-Guided Diabetic retinopathy screening
authors: Feng, Yubin; Zhou, Shuqing; Xu, Jiayao; Qiu, Weiwen; Zhang, Qiuli; Luo, Lianxiang
abstract: Background: Deep learning for diabetic retinopathy (DR) screening often degrades under variable image quality, domain shift, and overconfident errors. We developed and externally validated a deployment-oriented framework for calibrated, uncertainty-guided DR grading and referral triage. Methods: The system used a retinal MAE-ViT foundation encoder with leakage-controlled EyeQ quality-aware pretraining, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), and a soft ordinal objective for ICDR 0–4 grading. The reported inference configuration averaged four deterministic views within each of five independently trained seeds. Seed-specific temperature scaling, ordinal/referral thresholds, and selective-prediction rules were fitted only on the internal calibration split and then fixed before internal test and external validation. Results: The final five-seed TTA = 4 ensemble achieved internal accuracy 0.744, macro-F1 0.442, and QWK 0.724; external QWK was 0.782 on APTOS-2019, 0.690 on MESSIDOR-2, and 0.509 on DDR. RDR AUROC ranged from 0.873 to 0.970 and STDR AUROC from 0.803 to 0.977. At 90% target coverage, ensemble predictive entropy retained 89.5% of internal test cases with selective QWK 0.740. Under a 5% calibration missed-STDR rule, 75.7% of cases were automatically handled with a 2.6% missed-STDR rate. Corrected matched analyses did not show a consistent downstream advantage from quality pretraining. Matched baselines showed a deployment trade-off rather than a universal ranking claim. Conclusion: The framework provides a calibrated deployment evidence chain linking ordinal grading, referral discrimination, locked thresholding, uncertainty triage, matched baseline comparison, and post-hoc interpretability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Confident and Trustworthy Model for Fidgety Movement Classification
authors: Morais, Romero; Le, Thao Minh; Tran, Truyen; Alexander, Caroline; Amery, Natasha; Morgan, Catherine; Spittle, Alicia; Le, Vuong; Badawi, Nadia; Salt, Alison; Valentine, Jane; Elliott, Catherine; Hurrion, Elizabeth M; Dawson, Paul A; Venkatesh, Svetha
venue: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
abstract: General movements (GMs) are part of the spontaneous movement repertoire and are present from early fetal life onwards up to age five months. GMs are connected to infants' neurological development and can be qualitatively assessed via the General Movement Assessment (GMA). In particular, between the age of three to five months, typically developing infants produce Fidgety Movements (FM) and their absence provides strong evidence for the presence of cerebral palsy (CP). To improve accessibility to the GMA, automated GMA solutions have been a key research area with proposed models becoming increasingly more accurate and interpretable. However, current models cannot gauge their ability to make decisions, which may lead to overconfident mistakes. To address this issue, we propose a Deep learning-based approach that not only classifies movements as fidgety or non-fidgety but also selectively abstains from classification when uncertain. Through two novel regularization losses, our model maintains a balanced coverage across the two movement types, which prevents bias toward an easy-to-classify subset of movements. We show that our proposed model learns to gauge its own confidence on movement classification, and our proposed regularization losses effectively ensure that the model maintains a similar confidence across movement types. We also show that the local movement abstentions have little impact on the video-level coverage and that relying on the most confident predictions improves the video-level performance. © 2013 IEEE.

title: Digital Twin Ready Predictive Risk Management of Subsurface Injection Nodes Using Mechanics Informed Cross Fault Machine Learning
authors: Akpabli, Godsway; Rahnema, Hamid; Marfo, William Apau; Hayford, Kelvin
abstract: Predictive monitoring of injection operations requires evidence that warning rules transfer across fault conditions and loading rates. We develop a seven-variable representation of mechanical, hydraulic, and acoustic measurements and retrospectively evaluate source-calibrated Watch, Mitigate, and Hold indicators over 60, 30, and 10 s horizons. A separate Mahalanobis gate measures similarity to the source states. The original cohort comprises 18 pressure-stage events from two rough specimens and one smooth specimen; an independent archive adds six slow-creep stage peaks from a fourth specimen. A pump-based reconstruction reproduces every original event and model input. In the original rough-to-smooth transfer, Watch and Mitigate intercepted 6/6 events, with median warning time s of 16.5 and 3.5 s. In reverse transfer, both indicators intercepted 12/12 events but produced 22.9 and 42.2 s/event of pre-horizon alert activity. Deleting one smooth-source event changed support coverage in the final 30 s to 19.7–88.6%. On the independent specimen, the unchanged rough-source Watch indicator intercepted 5/6 peaks, whereas Mitigate and Hold intercepted none. The smooth-source Mitigate indicator intercepted 6/6 peaks but was active before its horizon for 72.8 s/event. Despite these contrasting outcomes, the source-domain gates included 99.7–100.0% of external states. The contributions are reproducible event construction, source-only policy evaluation, calibration sensitivity analysis, and an independent laboratory transfer test. The results show that high empirical support does not establish transferable warning thresholds. They motivate further advisory evaluation with separate prediction and support outputs. Four specimens, retrospective processing, and the absence of field validation do not establish operational readiness. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Information Design Against Gaming and Learning Adversaries
authors: Gaikwad, Madhava
abstract: A principal who deploys a binary classifier with an abstention option must decide which queries the mechanism abstains on. The right choice depends on the adversary. A gaming adversary already knows the classifier and tries to manipulate features across the boundary, so the principal does best by abstaining on queries close to that boundary. The same boundary-localizing rule is the worst possible choice against a learning adversary who does not know the classifier: each abstention now tells the adversary that the boundary is nearby, which is enough to drive a binary search. We analyze this tension. The two natural defenses, abstaining at a fixed rate and abstaining near the boundary, are Blackwell-incomparable: neither can be simulated by post-processing the other’s responses. The number of queries needed to reconstruct the boundary to error ε is Θ~(d/ε) under the first defense and Θ(dlog(1/ε)) under the second, where d is the VC dimension of the classifier family and Θ~ suppresses factors polylogarithmic in d and 1/ε. The first rate is a worst case over query distributions; no reconstruction algorithm can close the gap at the distributions that attain it. We characterize the Pareto frontier between the two defense objectives, and confirm both rates on seven binary-classification tasks spanning tabular, image, and language-model-feature inputs: label-plus-counterfactual access extracts the boundary with up to 200× fewer queries than a published label-only baseline. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Sustainable hybrid text classification: Enhancing encoder-only language models with NLI-derived pseudo-examples
authors: Cosentino, Cristian; Folino, Francesco; Marozzo, Fabrizio; Pontieri, Luigi
abstract: Building accurate text classifiers using small labeled data is a critical challenge in production systems and high-stake applications (e.g., misinformation mitigation, clinical decision support). Organizations struggle with expensive data annotation costs and need solutions that can adapt to data drifts over time. Despite their amazing results, contemporary generative Large Language Models are unsuitable for production classification tasks due to their high computational demands and inconsistent predictions. To tackle these issues, this work introduces a lightweight modular framework combining an encoder-only LM with weak supervision from pre-trained Natural Language Inference (NLI) models. The NLI models are used as zero-shot annotators, forming an ensemble that generates pseudo-labels to augment the set of training examples. Unreliable pseudo-labeled instances are discarded by using an abstention-based mechanism, based on label agreement and risk-bounded rejection thresholds. The remaining pseudo-labeled data are used to fine-tune the encoder-only classifier with minimal training overhead. Major strengths of the framework are: (i) synergistic integration of complementary pre-trained models, (ii) a cheap abstention mechanism for improving pseudo-label quality, and (iii) small computational costs (thanks to the use of small LMs and few training data and fine-tuning epochs). Tests on fake news and depression detection datasets show that this approach achieves compelling performances despite using a fraction of the computational burden required by generative LLMs and state-of-the-art semi-supervised-learning methods. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: R-GCRED: a retrieval-grounded and calibrated risk estimation for depression prediction and screening recommendation framework
authors: Saidi, Firas; Almulla, Marwa
abstract: Early depression detection from textual narratives has advanced substantially with transformer-based language models and Large Language Models (LLMs). However, reliable screening-oriented decision support requires more than high predictive accuracy. Existing approaches often lack explicit symptom-level grounding, produce poorly calibrated confidence estimates, and provide limited safeguards against uncertainty and unsupported model-generated evidence. This paper introduces R-GCRED, a Retrieval-Grounded and Calibrated Risk Estimation framework for transparent, evidence-grounded, and uncertainty-aware depression risk estimation from text. R-GCRED employs ontology-guided retrieval to constrain LLM-based evidence extraction to clinically relevant symptom facets, producing structured and source-traceable representations that capture symptom identity, polarity, intensity, and supporting textual evidence. A dedicated evidence-verification mechanism further reduces the propagation of unsupported symptom assertions to downstream prediction. The verified evidence is subsequently processed by a dual-head architecture for joint depression-risk classification and severity estimation, followed by probability calibration, uncertainty-aware abstention, and cost-sensitive recommendation modeling. R-GCRED is evaluated on the DAIC-WOZ and CLEF eRisk benchmarks using participant-disjoint evaluation protocols and is compared against general-domain transformers, mental-health-adapted language models, evidence-based methods and LLM-based baselines. Across the evaluated benchmarks, R-GCRED consistently outperforms the compared approaches, indicating that its performance gains extend beyond those obtained against conventional transformer baselines. The framework achieves a Macro-F1 of 0.84, an AUC of 0.89, and an Expected Calibration Error of 0.038, while attaining an AUC of up to 0.90 under partial-observation early-detection settings. Results demonstrate that integrating retrieval-grounded symptom evidence, evidence verification, calibrated prediction, and uncertainty-aware decision modeling yields measurable improvements in predictive discrimination, confidence reliability and explanation traceability over the evaluated existing approaches. These findings establish the computational effectiveness of R-GCRED across the evaluated benchmark settings but do not constitute prospective clinical validation. © 2026 Saidi and Almulla.

title: Valuation by Absence: Modeling Evidentiary Gaps in Patent Value Assessment
authors: Moorthy, Amrutha; Raghuram, M.S.
venue: 16th ITU Kaleidoscope Academic Conference - AI and Frontier Technologies for Good, ITU K 2026 - Proceedings
abstract: Patent valuation frameworks typically rely on affirmative indicators such as standard declarations, clause-level mapping, citation activity, product implementation, and licensing history. Yet in litigation, licensing negotiations, and essentiality assessments, valuation outcomes are often shaped by what the record lacks. Missing standard mapping, absent teardown evidence, deployment opacity, or the absence of licensing comparables can materially narrow valuation confidence. This paper formalizes evidentiary absence as a first-class input to patent valuation. Using IN218255, IN240893, Wi-Fi/mmWave SEP examples, and judicial reasoning including Optis v Apple, we develop an absence-aware framework across technical, deployment, and economic evidence layers. The framework introduces ordinal evidence states, absent, semantic proximity, structured evidence, and corroborated evidence, to guide valuation responses ranging from full valuation to constrained range, high uncertainty, or abstention. The approach improves transparency, reproducibility, and auditability in patent value assessment. © 2026 International Telecommunication Union.

title: Detecting the Unknown: Retrieval-Augmented OOD Detection for Intrusion Detection
authors: Lira, Oscar G.; Marroquin, Alberto; To, Marco Antonio
venue: Lecture Notes on Data Engineering and Communications Technologies
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) commonly rely on a closed-world assumption, which restricts their ability to handle previously unseen or zero-day attacks. This limitation often leads to the misclassification of novel threats as known categories, reducing their effectiveness in real-world deployments. To address this issue, this paper presents retrieval-augmented OOD detection, a framework that combines Out-of-Distribution (OOD) detection with a FAISS-based retrieval mechanism built upon a ModernBERT-based architecture. Importantly, the framework performs retrieval-only operations to obtain nearest-neighbor statistics and uncertainty signals; no text generation is performed, distinguishing it from generative approaches. The proposed method replaces the traditional softmax classification layer with a prototype-based approach and integrates a FAISS-indexed knowledge base. This enables the system to classify known attack types, detect unknown threats through semantic similarity, and incorporate new information dynamically without requiring retraining. Experimental evaluation on a composite dataset derived from multiple real-world sources demonstrates that the fine-tuned retrieval-augmented OOD detection model achieves 99.87% detection of unknown attacks across all evaluated novel classes on our dataset. Through selective confidence deferral, known accuracy reaches 83.0%, demonstrating that the trade-off between known and unknown detection is tunable rather than fixed. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

title: Uncertainty-Driven Selective Prediction with Auditable Human Deferral for EEG Decoding of Participant-Rated Occupational Risk
authors: Shen, Xianlong; Zhang, Shu; Bao, Ziyi; Zhang, Yan
abstract: Large-language-model (LLM) layers are increasingly appended to electroencephalography (EEG) decoders, although their decision contribution is often unclear. We evaluate an uncertainty-driven architecture in which a calibrated EEG classifier predicts participants’ own four-level occupational-risk keypress ratings, a deterministic rule either retains or defers a prediction, and a template or optional LLM renders an auditable report. The objective is not to replace a previously published classifier benchmark on the shared EEG archive, but to evaluate downstream decisions from a fixed frozen-representation decoder. The analysis used 2634 response-inclusive 3 s epochs from 31 retained workers. Subject-grouped three-fold evaluation yielded balanced accuracy of 0.6336 (95% CI 0.5745–0.6622) and accuracy of 0.6875. Peak probability distinguished correct from incorrect predictions only moderately (AUC 0.6529), and the coverage-risk relationship was non-monotonic. At tau = 0.5, 71.49% of trials were retained (balanced accuracy of 0.6829); with illustrative under-estimation/over-estimation/deferral costs of 5/0.5/1, normalized cost fell from 0.5816 to 0.5363, but sensitivity analysis showed that benefit depends on the cost setting and threshold. A rule engine reproduced all evaluated LLM risk/deferral decisions, while a deterministic template matched the prespecified reporting checks; therefore, no decision-performance advantage of the LLM was demonstrated. The study supports cross-participant prediction within the shared experimental setting, not stimulus-disjoint generalization or objective workplace-risk prediction. Because response timestamps and actual supervisor decisions were unavailable, motor/visual confounding cannot be excluded and the human handoff remains a simulated policy rather than a human–AI team evaluation. © 2026 by the authors.

title: TrustDTI: Trustworthy Drug-Target Interaction Prediction via Evidential Deep Learning and Selective Abstention
authors: Jeon, Kyungmin; Park, Seongyun; Jeong, Daesik
abstract: Accurate prediction of Drug-Target Interactions (DTI) is a fundamental step in accelerating the drug discovery process and repositioning existing drugs. Although deep learning models have demonstrated significant potential in DTI prediction, they often suffer from overconfidence and produce unreliable predictions in out-of-distribution (OOD) or cold-start scenarios, posing substantial risks in critical biomedical applications. Furthermore, evaluating these models without rigorous control for data leakage - such as overlapping drug-target pairs between the training and testing sets - often leads to inflated performance metrics. To address these limitations we propose TrustDTI, which is a reliable DTI prediction framework built on an enhanced multi-modal architecture. TrustDTI extracts molecular features using a Hybrid Drug Encoder (combining pretrained KPGT and DrugGNN representations) and protein representations using a graph attention encoder that refines ESM-2 residue features over a residue contact graph derived from predicted 3D structures. A bidirectional co-attention block and gated channel fusion module capture complex inter-modal interactions. Crucially, TrustDTI introduces a Deep Evidential Head that models the output as a Dirichlet distribution, quantifying both the epistemic and aleatoric uncertainties. Coupled with a Selective Head, the model dynamically defers predictions on highly uncertain pairs. Evaluated under a rigorous cross-domain cold-start protocol on BindingDB and DAVIS with exact-match overlap removal, TrustDTI achieves the best Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) across all four cold-start settings; on the in-domain unseen-drug and unseen-protein splits of BIOSNAP, it attains the highest Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (AUROC) among all compared methods. More importantly, by abstaining from its most uncertain predictions the model substantially improves reliability, demonstrating that explicitly quantifying uncertainty yields trustworthy decisions in the high-stakes setting of drug discovery. © 2013 IEEE.

title: Mixed-Criticality, Carbon-Aware Task Scheduling for Smart-Grid Edge-Cloud Computing: A Simulation-Based Heuristic
authors: Bashir, Albashir; Qureshi, Ayesha Wasim; Malek, Mohd Fareq Abd
venue: Proceedings - 2nd International Conference on Modern Sustainable Systems, CMSS 2026
abstract: Smart-grid edge-cloud networks host computational workloads of sharply different operational criticality, from millisecond-sensitive protection and control functions to delay-tolerant analytics and forecasting. Existing scheduling approaches address this heterogeneity only partially: dual-priority service differentiation protects delay-critical tasks but ignores energy cost, while carbon and price aware temporal deferral improves sustainability but ignores task criticality. This paper proposes a lightweight scheduling heuristic that unifies both principles, guaranteeing critical tasks unconditional first claim on compute capacity while deferring flexible tasks toward loweremission, lower-cost execution windows using a fast range-minimum lookahead over short-term carbon and price forecasts. The heuristic is evaluated through a discrete-event simulation driven by real UK National Grid ESO regional carbon-intensity data across eight independently selected weekdays in 2023, with a workload arrival rate calibrated from the Alibaba 2018 Cluster Trace, benchmarked against four baselines, and validated through an ablation study, a weight-sensitivity analysis, and a forecast-uncertainty experiment using the real FPN-BOA discrepancy distribution. The proposed heuristic eliminates critical-task deadline violations, reducing C O2 emissions by 22.9% and energy cost by 7.1% relative to an unaware baseline, all differences statistically significant at p<1 0-5 under paired t-tests. A carbon-aware earliest-deadline-first baseline achieves a larger raw reduction (48.8%) with zero violations, so the proposed method's principal contribution is a structural reliability guarantee that holds by construction, independent of arrival-pattern coincidence. © 2026 IEEE.

title: 28th International Conference on Pattern Recognition, ICPR 2026
abstract: The proceedings contain 47 papers. The special focus in this conference is on Pattern Recognition. The topics include: Revisiting Human-in-the-Loop Object Retrieval with Pre-trained Vision Transformers; when Not to Answer: Evaluating Prompts on Reasoning Models for Effective Abstention in Unanswerable Math Word Problems; Mamba-VOS: Efficient Video Object Segmentation with Selective State Space Models; metapath-Driven Embeddings for Zero-Shot Object State Classification; evoStruggle: A Dataset Capturing the Evolution of Struggle Across Activities and Skill Levels; eva Optimizer: Escaping Low-Curvature Traps in Deep Learning; DGI: Time Series Anomaly Detection by Injection of Anomaly Prior; few-Shot Adaptive Open-Set Object Detection with Personalized Scene Generation; liteAugNet: A Lightweight Semantic-Guided Augmentation Network for Efficient Edge-Level Image Classification; EMASAM: a Computationally Efficient Sharpness-Aware Minimization via EMA-Guided Perturbations; MFANet: A Lightweight Network Combining CNN and Mamba for Medical Image Segmentation; Is Visual Realism Enough? Evaluating Gait Biometric Fidelity in Generative AI Human Animation; BugHunter: An Automated Game Test Framework with MARL-Based Data Collection and FDM-Based Bug Detection; ClipTBP: Clip-Pair Based Temporal Boundary Prediction with Boundary-Aware Learning for Moment Retrieval; ilov3Splat: Instance-Level Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Understanding in Gaussian Splatting; what Matters for Grocery Product Retrieval with Open Source Vision Language Models; ReCo-MIL: Rare-Enhanced Contextual Multiple Instance Learning; NLOS-MT: A Hybrid Mamba and Windowed Attention Transformer for Non-Line-of-Sight Imaging; Following the Teacher’s Footsteps: Scheduled Checkpoint Distillation for Domain-Specific LLMs; returnRateNet: Neural Network-Based Estimation of Size-Related Return Rates in Fashion E-Commerce; FuseDPT: Multi-scale and Multi-projection Model for Learning Depth in 360 ∘ C; DotGreedX: Combining Scoring-Based Technique and Greedy Search for GNN Explainability; cross-Modal Learning for Plankton Recognition; risk-Field Constrained Reinforcement Learning for Safe Autonomous Driving; MMFuser: Multimodal Multi-layer Feature Fuser for Fine-Grained Vision-Language Understanding; LLM-Guided Exploration for Sample-Efficient UAV Navigation.

title: When financial fine-tuning fails: A three-level detectability analysis of numerical hallucination in domain-adapted language models
authors: Li, Xiaodong; Liu, Peiwei
abstract: Financial large language models are increasingly deployed for summarization of reports and disclosures, where numerical hallucination poses significant practical risks. While prior work often attributes such hallucination to insufficient numerical reasoning, this assumption has not been systematically tested under controlled fine-tuning settings. In this paper, we conduct a cost-effective, controlled study of numerical hallucination in financial summarization across three model variants: a base instruction-tuned model, a domain language-adapted model (FT-A), and a numeracy-enhanced domain model (FT-A+B+C). We introduce a three-level detectability taxonomy distinguishing between overt hallucination (currency-denominated fabrication), covert-explicit hallucination (professional-convention numbers), and covert-implicit hallucination (ungrounded quantitative claims). Our results reveal that domain fine-tuning substantially degrades numerical restraint at all detectability levels. While the Base model maintains near-zero hallucination rates (5.4%), FT-A exhibits 82.5% overt hallucination and FT-A+B+C reaches 98%. Contrary to intuition, numeracy supervision amplifies rather than mitigates hallucination across all levels. We identify template injection—the insertion of memorized canonical values regardless of input content—as a primary hallucination mechanism in fine-tuned models. These findings demonstrate that numerical hallucination in financial summarization is driven by the degradation of numerical restraint through domain adaptation, not by insufficient numerical reasoning. We recommend that evaluation protocols assess hallucination across all detectability levels and that deployment practices include explicit mechanisms for grounding-aware generation or abstention. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: DCRA: Lightweight Downstream High-Error Risk Estimation for 3D Human Pose Lifting
authors: Yu, Junyi; Yao, Futian
venue: BDIMed 2026 - Proceedings of the 2026 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Intelligent Medicine
abstract: Detected 2D keypoint confidence is a detector-side quantity, but downstream 3D pose lifting fails in a different space: a joint can be confidently localized in the image and still induce a large 3D error after lifting. We introduce Downstream-Calibrated Risk Assessment (DCRA), a lightweight reliability head that estimates whether each output joint from a frozen MotionAGFormer 2D-to-3D lifter falls in the downstream high-error tail. DCRA uses detected-keypoint confidence, 2D geometry, temporal cues, and joint identity, then applies post-hoc Platt calibration to convert risk logits into binary high-error event probabilities. It does not modify the predicted 3D pose. On Human3.6M detected-2D inputs with the top 20% train-error threshold, DCRA raises high-error AUROC from 0.636 for raw confidence to 0.775 and AUPRC from 0.362 to 0.467. It also improves Brier score, Spearman risk-error ranking, and risk-coverage error over raw confidence, calibrated raw confidence, and a feature-free joint-prior control, while the joint prior attains slightly lower expected calibration error. Spearman and risk-coverage are ranking diagnostics against continuous 3D error, not claims of calibrated continuous uncertainty. Across three seeds, DCRA remains stable, with AUROC 0.77495 ± 0.00058. The risk head adds 19,977 parameters and increases measured latency by 4.19% over MotionAGFormer-base. These results support DCRA as a compact single-pipeline diagnostic layer for downstream high-error event risk, not as a pose-accuracy improvement, restoration method, or broad transfer result. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: GoGet: A multi-model multimodal assistive agent with Disagreement-Gated Grounding
authors: Shrivastava, Siddhant; Praveen, A Manicka; Meghjani, Malika
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Advanced Algorithms and Neural Networks, AANN 2026
abstract: GoGet is a locally hosted multimodal AI agent. It composes four open transformer-family models on one NVIDIA RTX 5090 with 32 GB of VRAM and coordinates them through a shared textual working memory. The four models are Parakeet TDT 0.6B for speech recognition, Gemma-4 as the vision-language reasoner and controller, SAM 3.1 for open-vocabulary segmentation, and Kokoro-82M for speech synthesis. On each turn the agent perceives, routes the request across five operating modes, invokes the matching model or tool, observes the result, and re-plans. Our main contribution is Disagreement-Aware Grounded Fusion (DAGF), a selective-prediction policy for visual counting that treats the segmenter's count as authoritative only when the segmenter and the reasoner corroborate, and abstains with a hedged answer when they disagree. We evaluate on the live system. With exact ground truth, grounding raises counting accuracy from 0.37 to 0.91; on 260 real COCO images the gain is smaller (0.30 to 0.37), since counting real clutter is hard for both models. DAGF does not improve the count itself; it decides when to trust it. Cross-model agreement predicts a correct count (0.70 when the models agree, 0.23 when they disagree), and abstaining on disagreement more than halves confidently-wrong counts, from 0.63 to 0.25 (p < 0.001); the agent then returns a confident correct count on a third of queries and abstains on the rest. A cross-validated confidence floor (DAGF-R) cuts confident errors further on moderate counts (0.26 to 0.14). The intent router reaches a macro-F1 of 1.00, against 0.85 for a keyword baseline. We also embody the agent on a simulated mobile robot. Grounded counting is viewpoint-dependent: a far view is unreliable (0.30 exact-match) while a near view is exact (1.00), so the agent reads DAGF's abstention as a cue to approach before it reports. Every model is open and runs on a private GPU, so no audio, imagery, or screen content leaves the machine. © 2026 IEEE.

title: A controlled framework for chemistry-shift evaluation in descriptor-based materials screening
authors: Chen, Hongyi; Ye, Terry Tao
abstract: Descriptor-based machine-learning models are widely used for property prediction and screening in cheminformatics and materials informatics, but random-split benchmarks do not by themselves establish reliability when target chemistry is absent from training. This issue is especially relevant in composition-only materials screening, where models use elemental identities and stoichiometric proportions without crystal-structure information. This work introduces a controlled framework for chemistry-shift evaluation that separates training-volume loss, target-regime displacement, and feature-space novelty. The framework combines family-held-out splits, size-matched random controls, target-distribution analysis, interval-calibration stress tests, detector complementarity, and selective abstention. Applied to XGBoost with Magpie descriptors on MatBench band gap ( N = 4604) and phonon peak frequency ( N = 1265), it shows that withholding a single element family increases MAE by up to +461% beyond matched controls. Conformal coverage falls from 89% to 41% for halogens at 90% nominal coverage, while uncertainty-guided abstention reduces retained MAE by 14–47%. Chemistry-shift evaluation therefore provides a reproducible protocol for determining when descriptor-based screening is transferable, unreliable, or suitable for uncertainty-guided triage. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: Ghost Rider-Anomaly Aware Hybrid Reservation and Self-Deferral Framework for 5G/B5G Unlicensed in the 5GHz Spectrum Band
authors: Rahman, Md Rashedur; Costa, Paulo
abstract: Listen-before-talk (LBT) requirements for cellular operation in the 5 GHz band introduce challenges for preserving the traditional, scheduled channel-access paradigm. Gap-based LBT schemes may improve fairness in heterogeneous NR-U/Wi-Fi coexistence, but they also expose predictable slot boundaries that can potentially be exploited by adversaries. In this paper, we propose Ghost Rider, a resilient channel-access mechanism for 5G/B5G NR-U that uses anomaly-aware, randomized reservation signals (RS) to protect against CAD adversaries while preserving fairness for coexisting users. We analyzed the scheme with a discrete-time Markov chain (DTMC) model and validated it through simulation under active attacks. The simulation results show that Ghost Rider enables a victim NR-U to operate close to its nominal performance even at high attack intensities. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Leakage-guarded embedding compression and calibration for edge rice diagnosis
authors: Singh, Chatter; Singh, Amar; Dhelim, Sahraoui
venue: Digital Signal Processing: A Review Journal
abstract: Reliable diagnosis of rice diseases from field imagery requires more than strong performance on randomly partitioned data because near-duplicate leakage, calibration drift under image corruption, and edge-device constraints can each obscure practical utility. This study presents a leakage-guarded pipeline for compact, edge-oriented rice disease diagnosis. Perceptually similar images are grouped by perceptual hashing before group-disjoint train, validation, calibration, and test partitions are formed. A frozen EfficientNet-B0 backbone then produces 1280-dimensional embeddings, and a lightweight multilayer perceptron (MLP) head is trained with shift supervision, consistency regularization, and embedding-space MixUp. Multi-objective optimization selects a sparse embedding mask and head hyperparameters by balancing macro-F1, expected calibration error (ECE), field-shift performance, and a deployment-cost proxy. Temperature scaling fitted on a held-out calibration split supports selective prediction and an illustrative cost-aware recapture policy. On an expanded Paddy Doctor benchmark containing 29,538 images from 10 classes, the selected model retains 242 of 1280 embedding dimensions (18.9%) and achieves a macro-F1 of 0.948 (95% confidence interval: 0.942–0.954) on the leakage-guarded in-distribution test set, with an ECE of 1.12%. Under the most severe synthetic field shift considered, macro-F1 remains 0.857. These results indicate that sparse embedding selection can preserve most of the predictive performance of a tuned full-embedding head while reducing head-level complexity. Severe blur remains a major failure mode, and broader multi-site validation is required before agronomic deployment. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Evaluating large language models for selected public health research and practice tasks: A 100-question benchmark of reliability, workflow-assisted recoverability, and correct source-grounded abstention
authors: Li, Qingfeng; Cheng, Zhangbo; Cao, Feiyu; Wang, Xianglong; Bachani, Abdulgafoor M.
abstract: Background: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in public health, but performance on general-purpose benchmarks may not translate directly to routine, evidence-grounded public health tasks. Objective: To evaluate LLM performance on a selected sample of public health tasks, emphasizing first-attempt reliability, workflow-assisted correction, and correct source-grounded abstention. Methods: We evaluated 100 questions across literature-based factual extraction and summarization (n=56), vaccine-specific retrieval and absence detection (n=10), study design and sample-size calculation (n=27), and statistical analysis (n=7). Experiments were conducted during December 2024 to April 2025 with some rechecks performed in May-June 2026. Initial attempts generally used GPT-4o in public web interfaces; recognized failures were repeated with the same model or escalated to a more capable model. Responses were manually checked and graded against verified reference standards. Results: First-attempt accuracy was 72/100 (72.0%; 95% Wilson CI, 62.5%-79.9%): literature 53/56 (94.6%; 85.4%-98.2%), vaccine-specific retrieval 3/10 (30.0%; 10.8%-60.3%), study design 12/27 (44.4%; 27.6%-62.7%), and statistical analysis 4/7 (57%; 25%-84%). Among ten questions that required source-grounded abstention, 2/10 (20.0%; 5.7%-51.0%) were correct initially, including 0/7 (0%; 0%-35%) vaccine-specific items. All initial abstention failures were later corrected after repeat/escalation. Because retry/escalation continued after recognized failures, eventual correctness of 100% reflected the stopping rule rather than autonomous model accuracy. Conclusions: LLMs can assist selected public health tasks, but first-attempt reliability, task-specific validation, and source-grounded abstention remain critical for real-world use. © The Author(s) 2026. title: A lightweight reliability- and confidence-aware selective ECG framework for degraded remote monitoring
authors: Bilgehan, Nağme; Bilgehan, Bülent
abstract: Remote electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring in Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) systems is vulnerable to sensor noise, missing leads, packet loss, and temporal dropout. The proposed Lightweight Reliability-Aware Internet of Medical Things Electrocardiogram Network (LR-IoMT-ECGNet) is a lightweight reliability-aware framework that couples degradation-aware representation learning with selective decision support. Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt eXtended Large (PTB-XL) electrocardiography dataset version 1.0.3 was used with official folds for training (n = 17,418), validation (n = 2183), and independent testing (n = 2198). Robustness was evaluated under clean, mild, moderate, and severe simulated degradation. A hybrid gate combining predictive confidence and signal reliability was tuned exclusively on validation data and locked before test evaluation. The 24,429-parameter model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9188 and F1-score of 0.8449 under clean conditions and an AUC of 0.8683, sensitivity of 0.7753, specificity of 0.8004, and F1-score of 0.8089 under severe degradation. By contrast, clean-trained CNN and ResNet-1D baselines showed near-zero severe specificity (0.0252 and 0.0143). On mixed-quality test data, the hybrid gate retained 90.2% of records and achieved accuracy of 0.8412, sensitivity of 0.8026, specificity of 0.8973, and F1-score of 0.8569 among accepted cases. Confidence-only referral was marginally stronger on some metrics, indicating that predictive confidence is the dominant selective signal while input reliability provides complementary information. The results support a compact, degradation-aware selective ECG framework for edge- or gateway-assisted monitoring, while external wearable validation remains necessary. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: TRACE-Chem: Symmetry-Aware Counterfactual Reasoning over Typed Evidence Graphs for Verifiable Multimodal Chemical Record Extraction
authors: Liu, Jiaqi; Wang, Changshuai; Li, Hanshen
abstract: Automatically extracted chemical records can appear complete even when names, depictions, formulas, masses, and spectra disagree. Because databases consume records rather than evidence, such errors propagate silently. TRACE-Chem (Typed Relational Attestation with Counterfactual Editing for Chemistry) is an inference-time framework for verifying and repairing them. It organizes source-linked observations, candidate fields, and verifier outcomes in a Symmetric–Asymmetric Evidence Graph (SAEG) separating symmetric identity checks from directional scientific derivations. Counterfactual Localization and Dependency-Constrained Re-decoding (CLDR) masks candidate fault nodes to identify the view whose removal most restores coherence, then revises only dependency-affected fields. Executable checks and spectral compatibility feed a calibrated accept, repair, or abstain decision. On 124 open-access synthesis papers containing 1852 compound and 638 reaction records, TRACE-Chem achieved 84.3% canonical-record hard-match F1, 9.7 percentage points above the same extractor without verification. Against a single-pass multimodal baseline, invalid structures fell from 10.8% to 0.8%, unsupported fields from 14.3% to 2.4%, and expected calibration error from 0.281 to 0.052. Removing derivation direction lowered fault-localization accuracy from 91.2% to 82.8%; removing dependency discounting raised the unsafe-edit rate from 2.4% to 4.1%. Explicitly modeling relational symmetry and asymmetry therefore improves verifiability, calibration, and repair safety in multimodal chemical extraction. © 2026 by the authors.

title: TrustSpec: Simulation-Grounded Physics-Driven Spectral Inversion With Uncertainty Quantification for SiC Epitaxial Thickness Metrology
authors: Nie, Zijie; Yang, Shunlin; Guo, Qingjie
abstract: Accurate thickness metrology is essential for silicon carbide (SiC) epitaxial layers, yet classical Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) fringe analysis relies on artifact-specific preprocessing, degrades below the fringe-resolution limit, and provides no calibrated confidence for individual measurements. This paper presents TrustSpec, a simulation-grounded, physics-driven spectral inversion framework intended as a proof of concept for trustworthy SiC epitaxial thickness metrology. A dispersive two-interface interference model with randomized instrument disturbances is used as a spectral digital twin to generate labeled training spectra, and the same twin is reused at inference time as an analysis-by-synthesis referee. A deep ensemble estimates thickness from a physics-conjugate Fourier-magnitude optical-thickness representation; the ensemble sample standard deviation and a windowed re-synthesis consistency ratio define a two-channel trust plane for release, review, or rejection. In a reproducible simulation study over 0.4–25 μm, TrustSpec achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.110 μm and remains effective below 1 μm, where a classical FFT pipeline fails. Split-conformal recalibration yields 94.6% empirical coverage for a nominal 95% interval. The combined trust policy releases 90.5% of in-distribution spectra at an MAE of 0.066 μm and rejects all 600 tested simulated 28–38 μm thickness-extrapolation spectra; a 25–28 μm test shows a gradual rejection transition near the training boundary. Channel ablations, referee-window sensitivity, shifted-nuisance stress tests, and model-mismatch experiments delimit the scope of these simulation results and motivate batch residual monitoring, reference-wafer checks, and periodic two-angle acquisition for drift detection. Validation on measured SiC wafers remains necessary before production deployment. © 2026 The Author(s). Engineering Reports published by John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.

title: CerviTwin: An IoT-Enabled Prespecified Edge–Cloud Protocol for Pathology–Genomics Fusion in Cervical Cancer Immunotherapy
authors: Bai, Hua; Zhou, Bohui; Shang, Haixia; Lu, Na
abstract: Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) infrastructures can distribute pathology–genomics processing, yet no sufficiently powered public cohort links pretreatment cervical whole-slide images (WSIs), tumor RNA, and standardized immune-checkpoint-inhibitor outcomes. We present CERVITWIN, an IoT-enabled prespecified edge–cloud protocol. Hospital-edge processing converts quality-controlled tiles into 64 morphology prototypes while retaining raw images locally; a fixed pathway matrix produces 50 genomic tokens. A perturbation-stable sparse graph and reliability masks support incomplete-modality fusion. Heterogeneous response cohorts supervise a genomic teacher, but cross-domain distillation remains hypothesis-generating until a joint cervical cohort is available. Disjoint temperature and conformal-calibration sets govern prediction and deferral. TCGA-CESC, TIGER, and GSE205247 receive nonoverlapping analytical roles. Four protocol-verification experiments retain the reported numerical results for score, stress/calibration, graph-export, and payload-accounting checks; they are not target-domain clinical estimates or measured device/network results. The protocol fixes tensor dimensions, losses, provenance, endpoint, fault, security, and external-test rules. Clinical and deployed-IoT claims require frozen multi-institution data and repeated hardware, network, energy, and privacy measurements. © 2014 IEEE.

title: Field-Scale Techno-Economic Assessment and Real Options Valuation of Carbon Capture Utilization and Storage—Enhanced Oil Recovery Project Under Market Uncertainty
authors: Liu, Chang; Li, Cai-Shuai; Zheng, Xiao-Qiang
abstract: This study develops a field-based techno-economic model and decision framework for a CO 2 -enhanced oil recovery and storage project under joint market uncertainty. Historical drilling and completion expenditures calibrate investment cost functions, and three years of production data are fitted with segmented hyperbolic Arps curves to forecast 20-year oil output. Markov-chain models jointly generate internally consistent pathways for crude oil, ETA, and purchased CO 2 prices, which are embedded in a Monte Carlo valuation. The framework outputs probability distributions of NPV and deferral option value; under the mid scenario, their mean values are USD 18.1M and USD 2.0M, respectively. PRCC-based global sensitivity analysis identifies the dominant value drivers as oil price, CO 2 price, utilization factor, oil density, pipeline length, and injection volume. Techno-economic boundary maps in the joint oil and CO 2 price space then delineate feasible regions and break-even thresholds for key design parameters. Results indicate that CCUS-EOR viability cannot be inferred from oil price or any single cost factor alone, but requires coordinated consideration of subsurface constraints, engineering configuration, and multi-market dynamics, including the value of waiting in unfavorable regimes, contributing to low-carbon development and sustainable energy transition objectives. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Reject-Option Ensemble Learning for Neural Network-Based Channel Equalization
authors: Almeida, Wellington D.; Neto, Ajalmar R. Rocha
venue: 2026 IEEE Conference on Artificial Intelligence, CAI 2026
abstract: This paper introduces a selective ensemble of Extreme Learning Machines (ELMs) with reject option for nonlinear channel equalization. Traditional neural and metaheuristicbased equalizers often suffer from high computational costs and reduced reliability when the received signal is heavily distorted. Although ELMs offer fast analytical training, conventional ensembles treat all base models equally, allowing uncertain predictions to propagate through the decision process. The proposed method combines the speed and structural diversity of ELMs with a confidence-based rejection mechanism that suppresses low-reliability symbol estimates. Only high-confidence models contribute to the final decision, enabling the ensemble to adapt dynamically to challenging channel regions. Experimental results across four nonlinear channel configurations show that the proposed approach achieves lower bit-error rates than conventional ELMs, nature-inspired metaheuristic equalizers, and heterogeneous neural-network ensembles with reject option. The method also provides substantial computational savings, requiring only a linear training cost relative to the number of ELMs and less effort than gradient-based neural ensembles. © 2026 IEEE.

title: An Uncertainty-Aware and Explainable Feature-Fusion DenseNet for Cotton Leaf Disease Classification Using Monte Carlo Dropout and Grad-CAM
authors: Roy, Partha Jyoti; Islam, Faisal; Himel, Hrithik Mohanto; Islam, Abirul; Sourov, Sariful Islam
venue: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Quantum Photonics, Artificial Intelligence and Networking, QPAIN 2026
abstract: The accurate and reliable identification of diseases in cotton leaves is crucial for improving crop productivity and preventing excessive pesticide usage. Although deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated outstanding accuracy in disease classification, existing methods often fail to incorporate uncertainty into deterministic predictions and lack explainability. In this regard, this paper introduces an uncertainty-aware and explainable feature fusion DenseNet architecture for classifying diseases in cotton leaves. The proposed architecture utilizes double global feature fusion through Global Average Pooling and Global Max Pooling to extract complementary information of diseases, and then uses the Squeeze-Excite attention mechanism to enhance channelwise feature discriminability. Monte Carlo uncertainty estimation is introduced to support selective prediction to enhance reliability. Specifically, confidence-weighted GradCAM is developed for a reliable visual explanation corresponding to prediction confidence. Thorough experimental evaluations conducted on a cotton leaf disease image dataset clearly verify that our proposed framework outperforms conventional CNN architectures in terms of accuracy, reliability, and explainability. Uncertainty-aware selective prediction mechanism significantly reduces the risk of misclassification errors, while confidence-aware visual explanation offers valuable information about the relevant regions with respect to the disease. This indicates the feasibility of the proposed framework to be applied in real-world agricultural decision support systems, which demand accurate and explainable predictions. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Probabilistic Orchestrator for Indeterministic Multi-Agent Systems in Real-Time Environments
authors: Bovshover, Arkady; Kojukhov, Andrei; Levin, Ilya
abstract: Multi-agent perception systems must operate under fundamental asymmetries: some agents provide fast but unreliable observations, while others deliver higher-quality evidence with delay and uncertain correspondence. Traditional deterministic orchestration and rule-based fusion struggle to manage these trade-offs, often producing brittle or unstable behavior. We introduce a probabilistic orchestration framework that treats coordination as an epistemic generation problem—constructing and updating belief states under uncertainty—rather than a selection problem. Instead of committing to a single agent’s output, the orchestrator constructs a belief state that explicitly represents uncertainty, evidential provenance, and temporal relevance. Decisions are produced through latency-aware, association-weighted fusion, and uncertainty itself becomes a first-class signal governing action, deferral, and learning. Crucially, the orchestrator enables controlled teacher–student adaptation: high-confidence, well-associated stationary observations are gated into a feedback loop that improves ego perception over time while mitigating error amplification. We demonstrate the approach on an infrastructure-assisted dual-camera obstacle-recognition task. Experimental results show improved robustness to distance, occlusion, and delayed evidence compared to ego-only and deterministic orchestration baselines. By operationalizing orchestration as epistemic generation, this work provides a unifying framework for robust decision-making and safe adaptation in multi-agent systems, with implications that extend beyond perception to agentic and generative AI architectures. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Coverage-Constrained Selective Prediction for Short-Horizon Cryptocurrency Event Contracts via Adaptive Quantile Thresholds
authors: Hao, Zehui; Chen, Hang; Qi, Rui
abstract: A fixed-odds contract on short-horizon price direction has a positive expected value only when its win probability exceeds the break-even rate implied by the payout ratio. A deployable predictor must also produce signals at a sufficiently stable rate. We formulate this setting as selective prediction with a coverage constraint and combine a five-seed gradient-boosting ensemble over a 90-dimensional causal feature panel with daily adaptive quantile thresholds, each estimated from the preceding 14 to 28 days of model scores, with parameters selected on training data alone. Configurations are frozen after three chronological pseudo-out-of-sample folds and evaluated on a held-out period from 1 January to 10 June 2026, and the whole procedure is then repeated on a quarterly re-freezing cadence over seven successive windows. Across BTC and ETH at 5- and 10-min horizons, with a payout of 0.8 and a 55.56% break-even rate, the models execute 10.4 to 11.0 trades per day, and all four selective win rates exceed break-even. Under a dependence-aware block bootstrap, three of four remain significant, and within a 32-test confirmatory family, two survive Holm–Bonferroni correction. Coverage stays inside the operational band in 26 of 28 re-frozen windows. Compared under one execution protocol, a fixed calibration slice drifts out of band while a trailing window does not, and adaptive conformal inference (ACI) matches the proposed rule on coverage when its step size is tuned but not otherwise, whereas an outcome-driven conformal controller reduces coverage by more than an order of magnitude. The expected value is insensitive to exchange fees, which consume under 5% of the measured edge, and sensitive to the payout term. Under matched feature sets, training pools, and coverage, most of the apparent cross-asset difference does not persist. This paper presents a proof of concept for the framework rather than making any claim about cryptocurrency predictability. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Brain-Tumor Type Classification From MRI: Segmentation-Guided ROI, Conformal Prediction, and Selective Abstention Under Distribution Shift
authors: Nguyen, Ngan V. T.; Van Huynh, Tuan; Van Dang, Liet
abstract: Reliable classification of brain-tumor type from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is essential for treatment planning and patient management. While deep neural networks achieve high accuracy on this task, they typically produce point predictions without a measure of reliability, and their confidence need not fall when image quality departs from the training distribution. An uncertainty-aware classification framework is presented that couples segmentation-guided region-of-interest (ROI) localization with post-hoc calibration, split-conformal prediction, and selective abstention: a U-Net localizes the tumor; the cropped region is classified; and the prediction is equipped with a calibrated confidence, a conformal set with a distribution-free coverage guarantee, and a deferral rule that abstains on unreliable inputs. All experiments used the Figshare brain-tumor dataset under leakage-free patient-level cross-validation. ROI localization improved patient-level balanced accuracy from 93.8% to 96.1% with a predicted mask while also improving calibration, and the 90% conformal coverage held under deployment with a predicted mask. Under bias-field, blur, and gamma corruptions, where exchangeability no longer holds, the empirical coverage degraded but was restored by recalibration and patient-aware inference, while the abstention rate rose with severity. The exchangeable unit for a valid guarantee is shown to be the patient, not the slice: slice-level calibration met the intended per-patient coverage in only 27% of resampled splits, versus 84% for patient-level calibration. The reliability layer further transfers to a four-class benchmark that adds healthy scans. © 2013 IEEE.

title: A Didactical-Driven Teacher Assistant for a Dimensional Modeling Course
authors: Brisson, Laurent; Segarra, Maria Teresa; Smits, Grégory
venue: International Conference on Computer Supported Education, CSEDU - Proceedings
abstract: Educational chatbots powered by large language models (LLMs) show promising effects on learning outcomes, yet most systems delegate pedagogical decisions such as content selection and didactic structuring implicitly to the LLM, making tutoring strategies difficult to trace, evaluate, and reproduce. This paper presents a didactical-driven teacher assistant for a French-language university course on dimensional modelling, operating without commercial LLM budget or GPU infrastructure. The architecture formalises the instructor’s pedagogical reasoning into deterministic modules that handle intent detection, concept linking, and didactic approach selection before any text is generated; the LLM acts solely as a linguistic executor. Evaluation on 195 authentic student questions addresses two research questions. First, we show that standard semantic retrieval alone does not reliably recover the pedagogically required content, thereby justifying the upstream orchestration strategy adopted in our architecture (RQ1). Second, compared to free-tier LLMs whose detection performance varies widely across models and which produce errors silently, the deterministic pipeline achieves high pair precision (73%) with full traceability and explicit abstention, though its limited coverage confirms that the detection strategy requires further refinement (RQ2). Copyright © 2026 by SCITEPRESS - Science and Technology Publications, Lda.

title: 7th Workshop on Uncertainty for Safe Utilization of Machine Learning in Medical Imaging, UNSURE 2025, held in conjunction with 28th International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer Assisted Intervention, MICCAI 2025
abstract: The proceedings contain 22 papers. The special focus in this conference is on Uncertainty for Safe Utilization of Machine Learning in Medical Imaging. The topics include: Unsupervised Artifact Detection and Quantification via Contrastive Learning with Noise Reference; Disagreement-Driven Uncertainty Quantification in Late Gadolinium Enhancement Cardiac MRI; is Uncertainty Quantification a Viable Alternative to Learned Deferral?; evaluation of Uncertainty-Aware Multi-software Ensembles for Hippocampal Segmentation; numerical Uncertainty in Linear Registration: An Experimental Study; SPARTA: Spectral Prompt Agnostic Adversarial Attack on Medical Vision-Language Models; label-Free Estimation of Clinically Relevant Performance Metrics Under Distribution Shifts; out-of-Distribution Detection in Medical Imaging via Diffusion Trajectories; SCORPION: Addressing Scanner-Induced Variability in Histopathology; LEXU: Learning from Expert Disagreement for Single-Pass Uncertainty Estimation in Medical Image Segmentation; decoupling Clinical and Class-Agnostic Features for Reliable Few-Shot Adaptation Under Shift; aleatoric Uncertainty Medical Image Segmentation Estimation via Flow Matching; multi-Rater Calibration Error Estimation; pseudo-D: Informing Multi-view Uncertainty Estimation with Calibrated Neural Training Dynamics; metric-Guided Conformal Bounds for Probabilistic Image Reconstruction; evaluation of Monte Carlo Dropout for Uncertainty Quantification in Multi-task Deep Learning-Based Glioma Subtyping; benchmarking Uncertainty and Its Disentanglement in Multi-label Chest X-Ray Classification; uncertainty-Aware Classification: A Human-Guided Bayesian Deep Learning Framework; Empirical Bayesian Methods and BNNs for Medical OOD Detection; a Proper Structured Prior for Bayesian T 1 Mapping.

title: Uncertainty-aware face image quality assessment via heteroscedastic Gaussian modeling and parameter-efficient fine-tuning
authors: Guo, Jiateng; Zhu, Keyu; Jiang, Meilan
abstract: Face image quality assessment (FIQA) is an important preprocessing stage in face recognition systems. However, most existing methods output only a deterministic quality score and therefore do not characterize the reliability of individual predictions; fully fine-tuning a Vision Transformer backbone is also computationally expensive. To address these limitations, we combine parameter-efficient fine-tuning with heteroscedastic Gaussian modeling. The method unfreezes only the top two Transformer blocks, the final normalization layer, and a dual-output quality head of ViT-FIQA, and predicts the quality mean and variance using a bounded heteroscedastic Gaussian negative log-likelihood. The trainable parameters account for 8.29% of the full checkpoint. On CGFIQA-40 K with three random seeds, the model achieved an SRCC of 0.8030, compared with 0.8043 for the MSE baseline. Relative to the homoscedastic model, the Gaussian negative log-likelihood decreased from −1.585 to −1.714; empirical coverage of the 90% prediction interval was 89.65%, while mean interval width decreased by 26.3%. The pAURC 0.2 based on predictive variance was 0.0590, outperforming the 0.0736 obtained with random rejection. These results indicate that the proposed method provides sample-level uncertainty useful for risk ranking and calibration while retaining comparable point-prediction performance with a reduced trainable-parameter count and recorded peak allocated GPU-memory requirement under the reported setup. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

title: TriSV-CD: Selective verification with a do-no-harm arbitration gate for reliable remote sensing change detection
authors: Wang, Zhenyu; Shi, Gang
abstract: Vision–language models (VLMs) can diagnose disputed regions in remote sensing change detection (CD), but placing their prompt-sensitive decisions on an automatic correction path creates a reliability risk. We audit this behavior with Qwen2.5-VL models and find that direct accept/rollback outputs vary with prompt wording, while descriptive labels remain useful for error analysis but also vary with context and model scale. We therefore separate offline VLM diagnosis from deployment-time arbitration and propose V4-Safe, a training-free rollback gate for a test-time-augmentation correction proposal. V4-Safe measures the baseline probability on the proposal’s edit support and restores the baseline when that support lies in a high-confidence region; it requires no VLM inference at deployment. Across a complete five-backbone by three-dataset matrix, V4-Safe yields positive mean F1 changes in 13 cells, an exact no-op in one degenerate cell, and a statistically indistinguishable (Formula presented) change in one cell; 9 of 15 gains remain significant after Holm correction.
